[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p378/r1] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās says the debt-documentation verse was revealed specifically concerning forward sales (salam); Ibn ʿAṭiyya says such sales in Medina occasioned it, but the rule covers all debts by consensus.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p378/r2] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Adding “with a debt” disambiguates tadaayantum, since Arabic can use it for mutual repayment; an expressly specified term rules out an unknown maturity date.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p378/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · الربيع | reports | Al-Rabīʿ says documentation was initially made obligatory by the command, then lightened by the trust exception in 2:283. | mentions 2:283
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p378/r4] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · الشعبي | reports | Al-Shaʿbī, Ibn Jurayj, and Ibn Zayd report the view that “if one of you trusts another” abrogates the documentation command; a report attributes the position to Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī. | mentions 2:283
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p378/r5] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · جمهور العلماء | reports | Most scholars treat writing as recommended protection of property and removal of doubt; it does not harm a pious debtor and protects the creditor against an unreliable one.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p378/r6] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | prefers | The sound view is that witnessing makes a transaction prudent while mutual trust leaves room; no abrogation follows, because documentation is recommended as a precaution for rights people may waive, and 2:283 instructs debtors to repay when trusted. | mentions 2:283
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p378/r7] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · الطبري | reports | Al-Ṭabarī treats documentation as obligatory and argues that commands remain obligatory until evidence shows otherwise.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379#2/r1] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The debtor is ordered to dictate because testimony reflects his own acknowledgment; a written document he acknowledges functions as his dictation.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379#2/r10] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The three categories are distinct, though one person may have one, two, or all three traits; the classification follows Malik and other discerning scholars.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379#2/r11] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · بعض الناس | reports | Some say safīh means a young child, which the author rejects as mistaken.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379#2/r12] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · قوم | reports | Some say weak means an elderly fool; the author calls this a good interpretation.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379#2/r13] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The doubled form yamillu avoids a sequence of many consecutive vocal movements; the ungeminated form is a Qurayshi dialect.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379#2/r14] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | “With fairness” means truth and seeking what is correct.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379#2/r15] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · الطبري | reports | Al-Tabari takes the pronoun in “his guardian” to refer to the right/debt and cites reports from al-Rabiʿ and Ibn Abbas.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379#2/r2] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The debtor must be God-conscious while dictating and must not diminish any part of the right; baks is reduction through deception or evasion.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379#2/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Those ordered to dictate are legally competent persons managing their own affairs when present.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379#2/r4] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The verse then names three recurring categories that may need someone else to dictate for them.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379#2/r5] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | A safīh is someone with weak judgment about money who cannot manage either taking or giving; the term also applies when rights such as inheritance are apportioned.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379#2/r6] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Safīh is likened to loosely woven cloth; safah means lightness, as shown by Dhu al-Rumma’s poetic use of tasaffaht.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379#2/r7] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Under religious law, a financially incompetent safīh is under the guardianship of a father or appointed guardian.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379#2/r8] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | A “weak” person has impaired intellect or an innate deficiency and may likewise have a father or guardian.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379#2/r9] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | One unable to dictate is a minor, whose guardian is a father or trustee; it can also be an absent person, with an agent as guardian, and a mute is best classed as unable.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379/r1] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · عطاء | reports | ʿAṭāʾ and others say “let a scribe write” makes writing obligatory on the scribe; al-Shaʿbī and ʿAṭāʾ also specify that this applies when he is the only available scribe, while al-Suddī says it applies when he is free.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379/r2] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | “With justice” modifies the act of writing, not the noun “scribe”; a child, slave, or disfavored person can draft a sound document, though officials should use upright, trusted, knowledgeable document writers.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · مالك | reports | Mālik says only someone knowledgeable about documents, personally upright and trusted, should write them, citing the command to write justly.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379/r4] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · الزجاج | reports | The verb abā yaʾbā is irregular: among verbs with a fatḥa in the imperfect, this pattern normally occurs only when a guttural letter is involved; al-Zajjāj says the hamza resembles one.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379/r5] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · الربيع والضحاك | reports | Al-Rabīʿ and al-Ḍaḥḥāk, as transmitted by al-Mahdawī, say the prohibition on a scribe refusing was abrogated by the command not to cause harm in 2:282. | mentions 2:282
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379/r6] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | As Allah taught him can attach to “write” as the manner of writing, to “not refuse” as a reason to repay God's gift, or begin a new sentence that attaches to “let him write.”
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379/r7] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · القاضي أبو محمد | holds | No particular scribe must write if another is available, and he may decline unless hired; if none is available, an exhortatory duty falls on the present person. Documentation in general is recommended, like doing good in 22:77, and helps someone in need. | mentions 22:77
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p380/r1] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | rejects | He rejects an attribution to Ibn Abbas allowing a creditor to dictate a foolish debtor’s debt: it would impose an unproven liability outside the law; at most it could concern illness preventing dictation, which the verse does not mean.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p380/r2] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The emphatic form shahidayn suggests witnesses who have testified repeatedly, implying probity.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p380/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The phrase ‘from your men’ excludes unbelievers, children, and women, while its wording includes enslaved men.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p380/r4] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · شريح وإسحاق بن راهويه وأحمد بن حنبل | reports | These jurists allow an enslaved person’s testimony when he is upright, giving priority to the verse’s wording.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p380/r5] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · مالك والشافعي وأبو حنيفة وجمهور العلماء | reports | They disallow an enslaved person’s testimony, giving priority to the impairment of legal status.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p380/r6] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · الجمهور | prefers | The majority reads ‘if there are not two men’ as addressing a claimant who omitted two male witnesses, deliberately or through some excuse.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p380/r7] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · قوم | reports | Some read the clause as meaning that two men cannot be found, so two women may be summoned only when no men are available; the author calls this weak and says the wording favors the majority.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p380/r8] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | He gives three possible syntactic expansions for the nominative ‘a man and two women’: summon them, let them be, or have them testify; each supplies the governing verb for the purpose clause.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p380/r9] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · حميد بن عبد الرحمن | reports | He reports that some Meccans read imra’atān with a hamza followed by a quiescent alif.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p381/r1] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · ابن جني | reports | He explains the rare irre

gular quiescence of a moving hamza as successive lightening, first bringing it near a still sound and then making it a silent alif; the cited verse of poetry uses it for wa-anā.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p381/r2] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · الشاعر | reports | The cited line witnesses the form wa-anā in the phrase concerning the old man and poverty.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p381/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · أبو الفتح | reports | He calls the proposed explanation based on the hamza and alif sharing phonetic traits crude and unconvincing; he also cites Ibn Kathir’s ‘on their shins’ reading and ‘O you with a ring.’
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p381/r4] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Grammatically, ‘among those whom you approve’ modifies ‘a man and two women’; Abu Ali excludes ‘two witnesses’ from the adjective because its case differs, but the author says approval applies in meaning to both witness arrangements.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p381/r5] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · ابن بكير وغيره | reports | They take ‘among those whom you approve’ as an address to judges; the author says the address is to everyone, although judges handle the actual case.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p381/r6] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Because the verse speaks of witnesses whom people approve, it indicates that people are not presumed upright until their reliability is established.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p381/r7] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · حمزة | reports | Hamza alone reads inna tadilla with kasra on inna and fatḥa then kasra on the verb, and fataḏakkara with fatḥa on the ذ and nominative rāʾ; al-Aʿmash shares this reading.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p381/r8] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · الباقون | reports | The other readers use an open an in an taḍilla and make fataḏakkara accusative; Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr lighten its ذ and ك, while the others geminate them.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p381/r9] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The purpose clause does not mean that testimony is taken in order for a woman to err; two women are appointed so one can remind the other if she forgets. Sibawayh compares this construction to preparing a prop for a wall if it leans.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p382#2/r1] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · قتادة والربيع وغيرهما | reports | They read the summons as one to give initial testimony. The verse was revealed when a claimant sought witnesses among many people, who hesitated to come forward.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p382#2/r2] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · الحسن بن أبي الحسن وابن عباس | reports | They say the verse includes both accepting a request to establish testimony and accepting one to deliver testimony already held.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p382#2/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · مجاهد | reports | Mujahid limits the command to delivering testimony already acquired; al-Naqqash ascribes this interpretation to the Prophet. Initial witnessing remains voluntary, a view also reported from Lahik ibn Hamid, Ata, Ibrahim, Ibn Jubayr, al-Suddi, Ibn Zayd, and others.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p382#2/r4] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | prefers | He prefers al-Hasan’s inclusive reading: the verse recommends both forms of assistance. With ample witnesses and no danger to the right, a summoned person may decline for even a slight excuse; otherwise declining without excuse earns neither sin nor reward.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p382#2/r5] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | When necessity or a real risk of losing a right arises, the recommendation approaches obligation; if delay will certainly destroy the right, testimony is obligatory, especially when it was already acquired and the summons is to deliver it, as a trust owed.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p382#2/r6] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | La tasʾamu means ‘do not tire’; ṣaghīran and kabīran are circumstantial descriptions of the object, with the small item mentioned first for emphasis. Repeated debt recording could make people weary of writing.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p382#2/r7] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Aqsaṭ means ‘more just’; its comparative form is anomalous if derived from the quadriliteral, but may follow aqram from karam, with aqsaṭ meaning just and qasiṭ meaning unjust.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p382/r1] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The clause puts the cause before the intended result because listeners naturally seek the cause of events; this anticipatory order is an especially eloquent, concise alternative to a follow-up question and answer.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p382/r10] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · ابن القاسم عن مالك | reports | Another transmission from Malik permits women’s testimony in property, property agencies, and anything leading to property; Ashhab and others disagree, and the school has two positions when the testimony concerns a nonfinancial consequence.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p382/r2] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · أبو عبيد | reports | Abu Ubayd glosses taḍilla as ‘forget’; the author says a witness’s error is forgetting part and remembering part, whereas total forgetfulness is not called straying from testimony.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p382/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | For Hamza’s reading, an is conditional and the fa-clause is its answer; Sibawayh treats the raised verb as an adjective of the two women, though the author has reservations. The majority accusative coordinates with the verb governed by an.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p382/r4] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · ابن كثير وأبو عمرو | reports | Their light pronunciation of the kaf has the same sense as the doubled form, from the root meaning remembrance.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p382/r5] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · أبو عمرو بن العلاء وسفيان بن عيينة | reports | They interpret the light form as making the other woman’s testimony count as a man’s testimony; the author rejects this as distant and inelegant, saying remembrance is the fitting opposite of straying and the implied object is testimony.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p382/r6] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · الجحدري وعيسى بن عمر | reports | They read an taḍulla with ḍamma on ت and fatḥa on ض, meaning ‘forget’; al-Dani transmits this, while al-Naqqash reports another form with kasra on ض, meaning the testimony is lost.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p382/r7] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · حميد بن عبد الرحمن ومجاهد | reports | They read fataḏakkara with a light, kasra-bearing kaf and a nominative rāʾ.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p382/r8] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The verse permits two women’s testimony only when paired with a man.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p382/r9] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · ابن وهب عن مالك | reports | One transmission from Malik allows women’s testimony only in the debt matters specified by the verse or in matters only women can observe, by necessity.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p383#2/r1] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Because documentation can be burdensome, God removes blame for leaving immediate cash transactions unwritten; such dealings are usually small purchases rather than property. Al-Suddī and al-Ḍaḥḥāk define them as immediate hand-to-hand exchange.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p383#2/r2] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | An is accusative as a disconnected exception. “You turn it over between yourselves” implies possession transfers; land, houses, and much livestock cannot be handed over cleanly in the same way, so debt-like documentation suits them.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p383#2/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · عاصم | reports | ʿĀṣim reads tijāratan in the accusative; the other readers read it in the nominative, though Abū ʿAlī is unsure about Ibn ʿĀmir.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p383#2/r4] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | With nominative, kāna means “occur” and needs no predicate; with accusative, its event sense is absent and an omitted subject or predicate is supplied, such as “unless the transaction is a trade.”
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p383/r1] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | If aqwam means ‘more firmly establishing,’ it too is a comparative from a quadriliteral; deriving it from qāma, ‘to be upright,’ removes the irregularity.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p383/r2] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Adna means ‘nearer,’ and tartābū means ‘doubt.’
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p383/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي | reports | He reads yasʾamū, yaktubū, and yartābū with yāʾ throughout, reporting the absent parties’ speech.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p384/r1] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · أبو علي والمبرد | reports | Abū ʿAlī and al-Mubarrad transmit a poetic line with “if it were an awful day” using accusative yawm; al-Ṭabarī's variant has nominative, as does Sībawayh's version.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p384/r2] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · الطبري | reports | Al-Ṭabarī interprets “witness when you transact” as applying to transactions both small and large.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p384/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · الحسن والشعبي | reports | Al-Ḥasan, al-Shaʿbī, and others say witnessing a transaction is recommended; Ibn ʿAmr and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say it is obligatory, followed by Ibn ʿUmar's practice and ʿAṭāʾ, with al-Ṭabarī preferring obligation.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p384/r4] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · القاضي أبو محمد | prefers | Ibn ʿAṭiyya finds obligation untenable: witnessing tiny sales is burdensome, while larger dealings may rely on social trust or customary practice. He prefers recommendation unless an excuse prevents it.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p384/r5] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · قوم | reports | Some say witnessing is abrogated by the trust exception in 2:283; al-Mahdawī records this view and Makkī attributes it to Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī. | mentions 2:283
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p384/r6] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · الحسن وقتادة وطاوس وابن زيد | reports | They say “do not harm a scribe or witness” prohibits a writer from adding to or subtracting from what was dictated and a witness from altering testimony; Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and ʿAṭāʾ also understand it to prohibit their refusal.

[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385/r1] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · عمر بن الخطاب وابن مسعود ومجاهد | reports | They read the verb with the letters separated and the first rāʾ fatḥa, meaning a claimant may initiate harm to the scribe or witness; al-Ṭabarī reports and explains this reading accordingly.

[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · أبو جعفر بن القعقاع وعمرو بن عبيد | reports | They read the geminated rāʾ with sukūn in the jussive; Abū al-Fatḥ calls it questionable but explains it as treating connected speech like a pause.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385/r4] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · عكرمة | reports | ʿIkrima reads the first rāʾ with kasra and makes “scribe” and “witness” accusative, so that the rights-holder is forbidden to begin harming them.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385/r5] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · ابن محيصن | reports | Ibn Muḥayṣin reads the geminated verb with rafʿ; after Ibn Mujāhid questions it, Abū al-Fatḥ explains it as a negative statement meaning the scribe ought not to be harmed, supported by poetry. [IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385/r6] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | If harm means falsification by a writer or witness, fisq is the legal commission of grave sins and invalidating rights; if it means mistreatment or refusal, fisq means departing from what is right, though disobeying God's command approaches the legal sense too.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385/r7] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Bikum implies “a state of fisq upon you”; the close of the verse admonishes and recounts God's favor, and another interpretation promises that piety teaches a person what is good.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p47/r1] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · حذيفة بن اليمان | reports | Ḥudhayfa reports that, after transmitters and non-Arab readers spread across regions, Iraqi and Syrian groups disputed their readings in the Armenia campaign; some disavowed others’ recitations.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p47/r2] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · حذيفة بن اليمان | reports | On returning to Medina, Ḥudhayfa urged ʿUthmān to act on the Book before the community split like Jews and Christians; ʿUthmān agreed to intervene.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p47/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · عثمان بن عفان | reports | ʿUthmān appointed capable, learned, eloquent men to prepare a codex, choosing among transmitted variants the best-known Prophetic readings and most eloquent language.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p47/r4] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · عثمان بن عفان | reports | ʿUthmān instructed the scribes to use Quraysh’s language when they differed.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p47/r5] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Ibn ʿAṭiyya explains that if you differ concerns differences in transmitted readings; every one of the seven language forms in the Qurʾān must derive from the Prophet and have been recited to him.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p47/r6] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The community followed the selected codex and set aside variant codices to prevent further division and preserve unity.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p47/r7] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Ibn Masʿūd resisted replacing his codex, so it was left; scholars nevertheless barred reciting from it to prevent confusion, since explanatory notes were reportedly mistaken for Qurʾān.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p47/r8] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | No Qurʾānic meaning was lost when noncanonical wording was left out, because the meanings remain in the established text.
[TABRISI:2:282#2/r1] TABRISI, d. 548 · سيبويه | reports | A third analysis supplies an omitted predicate for the subject فرجل وامرأتان, understood as فرجل وامرأتان يشهدون. | mentions 5:95
[TABRISI:2:282#2/r2] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | On this analysis يشهدون governs أن; its omission is placed before the conditional with fatḥ and after it with kasra.
[TABRISI:2:282#2/r3] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The particle أن is accusative here, with the sense “because one woman may forget, then the other remind her.”
[TABRISI:2:282#2/r4] TABRISI, d. 548 · سيبويه | reports | Sībawayh says testimony is requested so one woman may remind the other; possible forgetfulness is the reason for reminding, like shoring a wall because it may lean.
[TABRISI:2:282#2/r5] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | reports | With the nominative reading, كان means “occur” or “happen,” so the phrase means that a present trade occurs.
[TABRISI:2:282#2/r6] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | reports | One analysis derives لا يضار from doubled ر, with the writer and witness forbidden to depart from the truth.
[TABRISI:2:282#2/r7] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | prefers | The first interpretation of لا يضار is clearer; Abū Jaʿfar's doubled quiescent rāʾ is unusual and explained by treating connected recitation like pause.
[TABRISI:2:282#3/r1] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | داينت and تداينت mean transacting in debt, either by borrowing or lending; the cited poem shows this usage.
[TABRISI:2:282#3/r2] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The verb دنت means borrowing while أدنت means lending; أمل and أملى are both used for dictating.
[TABRISI:2:282#3/r3] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | بخس is unjust diminution; safīh means ignorant or light-minded, named for the lightness of reason.
[TABRISI:2:282#3/r4] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The otherwise unusual pattern أَبَى يَأبى is explained by the hamza behaving like a guttural consonant.
[TABRISI:2:282#3/r5] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Ḍalāl originally means loss or going where something cannot be found; saʾam is weariness, and أقسط means acted justly while قسط means acted unjustly. | mentions 54:47
[TABRISI:2:282#3/r6] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The opening continues the previous direction to defer an insolvent debtor by explaining rules for deferred claims and debt transactions.
[TABRISI:2:282#3/r7] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | reports | بدين may reinforce the meaning of تداينتم; alternatively it distinguishes debt transactions from تداينتم understood as mutual requital. | mentions 6:38
[TABRISI:2:282#4/r1] TABRISI, d. 548 · الشعبي وجماعة من المفسرين | reports | Al-Shaʿbī and other commentators treat writing as a communal duty; al-Rummānī and al-Jubbāʾī choose that view.
[TABRISI:2:282#4/r10] TABRISI, d. 548 · القاضي | reports | Al-Qāḍī differentiates the three: the foolish person squanders, the weak person is an adolescent, and the one unable to dictate is insane.
[TABRISI:2:282#4/r11] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | reports | The debtor's guardian may dictate; alternatively, Ibn ʿAbbās says the guardian here is the creditor, who knows the debt best.
[TABRISI:2:282#4/r12] TABRISI, d. 548 · مجاهد | reports | Mujāhid limits the two male witnesses to free, adult, Muslim men; al-Ṭabrisī rejects freedom as a condition, requiring Islam and probity instead.
[TABRISI:2:282#4/r2] TABRISI, d. 548 · الجبائي | reports | Al-Jubbāʾī allows a scribe and witness to take payment, while al-Ṭūsī says their school does not permit it; paper costs belong to the creditor.
[TABRISI:2:282#4/r3] TABRISI, d. 548 · السدي | reports | Al-Suddī says a scribe must write when free of other work.
[TABRISI:2:282#4/r4] TABRISI, d. 548 · مجاهد وعطاء | reports | Mujāhid and ʿAṭāʾ say writing becomes obligatory when the scribe is asked.
[TABRISI:2:282#4/r5] TABRISI, d. 548 · الحسن | reports | Al-Ḥasan says refusal is obligatory to avoid only when there is no alternative scribe and refusal would harm the creditor; otherwise the scribe has latitude.
[TABRISI:2:282#4/r6] TABRISI, d. 548 · الضحاك | reports | Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says writing was originally obligatory but was abrogated by the ban on harming a scribe or witness.
[TABRISI:2:282#4/r7] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The command is emphasized because scribes were scarce in the Prophet's time; combining a command with a prohibition against neglect makes compliance more likely.
[TABRISI:2:282#4/r8] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The debtor dictates and must fear God, reducing neither the amount nor the quality of what is owed.
[TABRISI:2:282#4/r9] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | reports | The debtor may be a fool through ignorance, childhood, or impaired understanding; weak may mean intellectual disability or senility, and inability may mean madness, stammering, or muteness.
[TABRISI:2:282#5/r1] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | If two men are unavailable, the witness set is one man and two women whose outward probity and trustworthiness the parties accept; this makes justice a condition of testimony.
[TABRISI:2:282#5/r2] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The wording requires witnesses acceptable to the parties, since people cannot know whom God approves except from outward reliability and integrity.
[TABRISI:2:282#5/r3] TABRISI, d. 548 · الربيع والسدي والضحاك وأكثر المفسرين | reports | Most commentators take تضل as one woman forgetting the testimony she and the other woman heard; the light reading likewise means prompting her to recall it.
[TABRISI:2:282#5/r4] TABRISI, d. 548 · سفيان بن عيينة | reports | Sufyān b. ʿUyayna reads the doubled form as making one woman equivalent to a man; al-Ṭabrisī says the memory-based reading is stronger.
[TABRISI:2:282#5/r5] TABRISI, d. 548 · حسين بن علي المغربي | reports | Al-Maghribī says تضل concerns a lost or forgotten testimony, not a woman herself going astray; this avoids needless repetition of إحداهما. | mentions 7:37
[TABRISI:2:282#5/r6] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | reports | The repeated إحداهما may put the subject before its object and avoid separating verb and subject, or may clarify that a testimony is lost rather than a person straying.
[TABRISI:2:282#6/r1] TABRISI, d. 548 · مجاهد وعطاء وسعيد بن جبير | reports | One report

ed view says summoned witnesses must not refuse to give testimony they know without doubt, provided doing so causes them no harm.
[TABRISI:2:282#6/r2] TABRISI, d. 548 · قتادة والربيع | reports | Qatāda and al-Rabīʿ say the witnesses must not refuse when summoned to establish and carry the testimony.
[TABRISI:2:282#6/r3] TABRISI, d. 548 · ابن عباس والحسن | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan understand the summons as covering both bearing and delivering testimony; the author prefers this broader reading.
[TABRISI:2:282#6/r4] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Do not weary of recording a debt, small or large, until its term; this is fairer, steadier testimony, and less likely to leave doubts about amount or term.
[TABRISI:2:282#6/r5] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | reports | The command may address witnesses and mean not to tire of recording testimony; the stronger referent of its term is the debt's due date, not the witness's allowable period.
[TABRISI:2:282#6/r6] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Writing the debt or testimony is more just before God, more reliable for testimony, and closer to preventing doubt; قسط means fairness and الأقسط means acting justly.
[TABRISI:2:282#6/r7] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | A spot transaction exchanged hand to hand can be left unwritten because documentation is needed for deferred payment, not cash trade.
[TABRISI:2:282#7/r1] TABRISI, d. 548 · الحسن وجميع الفقهاء | reports | Al-Ḥasan and the jurists regard witnessing sales as recommended; the Ẓāhirīs make it obligatory.
[TABRISI:2:282#7/r2] TABRISI, d. 548 · الحسن وقتادة وعطاء وابن زيد | reports | With kasra on the first rāʾ, the prohibition addresses the writer and witness: do not change dictated terms, testify to matters not requested, or refuse to testify.
[TABRISI:2:282#7/r3] TABRISI, d. 548 · ابن مسعود ومجاهد | reports | With fatḥ on the first rāʾ, the prohibition tells people not to impose writing on a busy scribe or summon a witness when excused, or to mistreat either.
[TABRISI:2:282#7/r4] TABRISI, d. 548 · الزجاج | prefers | Al-Zajjāj says the first reading is clearer because deliberate falsification makes someone a wrongdoer more plausibly than summoning a busy witness does.
[TABRISI:2:282#7/r5] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The verse threatens that harming a scribe or witness in writing or testimony is a departure from God's commands; fear God, who teaches what is needed and knows all.
[TABRISI:2:282#7/r6] TABRISI, d. 548 · علي بن إبراهيم بن هاشم | reports | ʿAlī b. Ibrāhīm b. Hāshim's tafsīr counts five hundred legal rulings in al-Baqara and fifteen in this verse alone.
[TABRISI:2:282/r1] TABRISI, d. 548 · حمزة | reports | Ḥamza alone reads إن تضل with kasra, as a conditional particle whose جواب is فتذكر.
[TABRISI:2:282/r2] TABRISI, d. 548 · ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وقتيبة | reports | Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, and Qutayba read فتذكر lightly and in the subjunctive.
[TABRISI:2:282/r3] TABRISI, d. 548 · حمزة | reports | Ḥamza reads فتذكر with doubled dhāl and indicative mood.
[TABRISI:2:282/r4] TABRISI, d. 548 · الباقون | reports | The remaining readers read فتذكر with doubled dhāl and subjunctive mood.
[TABRISI:2:282/r5] TABRISI, d. 548 · عاصم | reports | ʿĀṣim alone reads تجارة حاضرة in the accusative; the others read it nominative.
[TABRISI:2:282/r6] TABRISI, d. 548 · أبو جعفر | reports | Abū Jaʿfar reads لا يضار with a doubled, quiescent rāʾ; the remaining readers use the doubled rāʾ in the accusative form.
[TABRISI:2:282/r7] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | For Ḥamza's conditional reading, رجل وامرأتان forms a nominative description of the two women, while ممن ترضون refers back to that nominative pair rather than accusative شهيدين.
[TABRISI:2:283/r1] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | reports | One analysis takes تداينتم as mutual requital, while another takes it as dealing in debt; adding بدين resolves this lexical ambiguity.
[TABRISI:2:283/r2] TABRISI, d. 548 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās says the verse was revealed specifically concerning forward sale and testifies that God permitted a guaranteed sale to a known term.
[TABRISI:2:283/r3] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | prefers | Although Ibn ʿAbbās specifies forward sale, the verse's apparent scope includes every deferred debt, which commentators and jurists accept.
[TABRISI:2:283/r4] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Writing the debt protects against forgetting or denial and secures the rights of creditor, debtor, and witnesses for the reasons explained.
[TABRISI:2:283/r5] TABRISI, d. 548 · أبو سعيد الخدري والحسن والشعبي | reports | Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, al-Ḥasan, and al-Shaʿbī say writing the debt is recommended, the majority's preferred view.
[TABRISI:2:283/r6] TABRISI, d. 548 · الربيع وكعب | reports | Al-Rabīʿ and Kaʿb regard writing as obligatory; the author cites the permission to rely on trust as evidence against obligation.
[TABRISI:2:283/r7] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | A just scribe records the debt or sale accurately, without changing its terms, amount, or anything that harms either party without consent.
[TABRISI:2:283/r8] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | reports | The scribe must not refuse to write; كما علمه الله may mean writing justly as God taught, or that the scribe must not hoard the skill God gave him.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p119/r1] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · علي بن عبيد الله | reports | Adnā is the elative form of d-n-w, meaning nearness or proximity.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p119/r2] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · ابن فارس | reports | Ibn Fāris distinguishes hamzated danīʾ, meaning low or inferior, from unhamzated danī, meaning near.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p119/r3] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · ابن فارس | reports | Ibn Fāris says the world is called al-dunyā because it is near, and gives dunyāwī as its relative form.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p119/r4] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · author | holds | Dānaytu bayna al-amrayn means bringing two matters close together; the hadith’s danū means eat what is nearest.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p119/r5] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · author | reports | In the debt verse, adnā means more likely or more conducive to avoiding doubt. | mentions 4:3, 5:108
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p194/r1] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · author | holds | Bayʿ is exchanging one item of property for another under specified terms.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p194/r2] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · author | holds | In Arabic, bayʿ may also mean buying; the cited line says to buy a cloak for a shepherd.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p194/r4] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · author | reports | One reported Qurʾānic sense of bayʿ is a contract of exchange. | mentions 2:275
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p263/r1] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · author | holds | Ḥuḍūr is the opposite of absence; ḥaḍar contrasts with the open countryside, and ḥaḍāra means settled urban life.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p263/r2] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · أبو زيد | reports | Abū Zayd pronounces ḥaḍāra with a kasra on the ḥāʾ.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p263/r3] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · الأصمعي | reports | Al-Aṣmaʿī pronounces ḥaḍāra with a fatḥa; a cited line illustrates the word.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p263/r4] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · author | holds | With ḍamma, ḥuḍur means an enemy.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p263/r5] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · author | holds | With fatḥa, ḥaḍar means a fortress; ʿAdī’s line supplies the usage.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p263/r9] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · author | reports | Ḥuḍūr can mean something immediately available or present, as with a spot transaction.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p267/r2] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · author | reports | Ḥaqq can mean money or property owed as a debt.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r1] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · علي بن عبيد الله | reports | Al-Dīn is what a person undertakes; religious commitment means undertaking what God requires.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r2] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · غيره | reports | Another definition makes religion divine speech that disciplines the self and restrains natural impulses.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r3] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · author | holds | Dīn can mean dominion: to dāna a people is to subdue them, and they then submit.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r4] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · ابن قتيبة | reports | Ibn Qutayba derives God’s dīn from this sense of domination and submission.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r5] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · القطامي | reports | Al-Quṭāmī’s line uses tadīnuka for making someone submissive.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r6] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · author | reports | A second cited line also uses dīn for an authority or condition of subjugation.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r8] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · author | holds | Dīn can mean worship, as shown by a poem asking whether this is always his and the speaker’s religion.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r9] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · author | holds | Dāyana means transacting by extending a loan; adāna means borrowing on debt.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p377/r1] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · author | holds | Shahīd means witness, related to shāhid as ʿalīm is related to ʿālim, and derives from witnessing.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p377/r2] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · author | holds | Testimony is reporting what one has witnessed; mashhad is a place where people gather.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p377/r8] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · author | reports | Shahīd can mean a witness testifying truth against the person testified against, including debt witnesses. | mentions 2:143
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p408/r3] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · author | holds | A Qur'anic use of ضل is forgetting, as in the case of one witness needing the other to remind her.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p571/r1] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · author | holds | Al-marʾa means an adult female descendant of Adam; al-marʾ means a man.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p571/r14] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · author | reports | Some add an unidentified woman, as in the debt testimony formula of one man and two women.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p336/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · الزجاج | reports | Al-Zajjaj says dāyantu means transacting with someone by taking a loan from him or lending to him; a cited line about Arwa illustrates settling debts.

BNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p336/r2] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | The command concerns a debt due at a specified term and requires writing and witnesses to protect property and people from injustice; documented proof restrains a debtor’s temptation to deny it.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p336/r3] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbas says the verse was revealed specifically about salam, an advance-purchase transaction.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p336/r4] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن الأنباري | reports | Ibn al-Anbari distinguishes tadāyantum for dealing, selling, or lending from dayn for recompense; the latter is pronounced with kasra, as in 51:12, and a cited poem illustrates recompense. | mentions 51:12
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p336/r5] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | Al-ʿadl means what is right; Qatada says to omit no rightful due and add nothing false.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337#2/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbas says the debtor cannot dictate because he is slow or tongue-tied; Ibn Jubayr says he cannot properly dictate what he owes, while Qadi Abu Yaʿla says he is insane.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337#2/r2] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn Jubayr, al-Rabiʿ, Muqatil, and Ibn Qutayba say the guardian is the creditor’s guardian, meaning the holder of the right.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337#2/r3] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · الضحاك | reports | Al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd say the pronoun refers to the debtor, so his guardian dictates.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337#2/r4] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · الزجاج | prefers | Al-Zajjaj prefers the debtor’s guardian: accepting the claimant’s dictation would leave no reason for writing and witnesses, and would simply accept the claimant’s word; Qadi Abu Yaʿla agrees.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337#2/r5] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | Al-ʿadl means fairness or equity.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337#2/r6] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · مجاهد | reports | Mujahid says “your men” means free men.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337#2/r7] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · الزجاج | prefers | Al-Zajjaj and Qadi Abu Yaʿla take “your men” to mean Muslims, supported by the verse’s opening address to believers.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · سعيد بن جبير | reports | Saʿid ibn Jubayr says a scribe must not refuse to write as God taught him the skill of writing; al-Shaʿbi calls writing a communal duty like jihad.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r10] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · مجاهد | reports | Mujahid and al-Suddi say “weak” means a fool.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r11] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · القاضي أبو يعلى | reports | Qadi Abu Yaʿla gives “minor” as a third meaning of weak.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r2] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · الزجاج | reports | Al-Zajjaj instead understands “as God taught him” to mean writing according to God’s command and truth.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r3] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · سعيد بن جبير | reports | Saʿid ibn Jubayr says the person owing the debt must dictate what he owes the claimant to the scribe and must not reduce any part of it.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r4] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | Amalla and amlā are two forms for dictating; the former is associated with the claimant repeating the statement at length.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r5] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · مجاهد | reports | Mujahid and Ibn Jubayr define the “foolish” debtor as ignorant about property and unable to dictate.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r6] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · الحسن | reports | Al-Hasan says the foolish debtor is a child or a woman.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r7] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · الضحاك | reports | Al-Dahhak and al-Suddi identify the foolish debtor as a minor.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r8] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · القاضي أبو يعلى | reports | Qadi Abu Yaʿla says foolish here means someone who squanders money.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r9] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn Jubayr explain “weak” as incapacitated, mute, or mentally unsound.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | “If the two are not men” means if the two witnesses are not both men, not if two men cannot be found.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r2] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbas says witnesses “whom you approve” are people of merit and religious integrity.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r3] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · الزجاج | reports | Al-Zajjaj says the construction means appoint two women so that one may remind the other, or for that purpose.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r4] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | reports | Hamza reads in tadhilla with kasra; here dalāl means forgetfulness, according to Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, al-Rabiʿ, Muqatil, and others.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r5] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | reports | Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr read fatudhakkira with a light kaf and accusative ra; Hamza reads it with a doubled kaf and nominative ra; the rest use doubled kaf and accusative ra.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r6] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · الضحاك | reports | The majority take the light and doubled readings alike: the second woman recalls the matter after the first forgets.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r7] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · سفيان بن عيينة | reports | Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna and al-Asmaʿi’s report from Abu ʿAmr take the light reading to make two women’s testimony equivalent to one man’s; Qadi Abu Yaʿla prefers this.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r8] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · أبو علي | rejects | Abu ʿAli rejects Ibn ʿUyayna’s view: no number of women’s testimony suffices without a man, and forgetfulness should be answered by a reminder.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339#2/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | Do not grow weary of recording small or large debts customarily deferred, through their due date; the document is more just, strengthens testimony by reminding witnesses, and more nearly removes doubt.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339#2/r2] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | The exception is an immediate exchange in which each party must deliver what it contracted for at once; ʿAsim reads tijāratan in the accusative, treating the funds as the commerce, and writing is waived to avoid burden in ordinary purchases.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339#2/r3] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | Witnessing is recommended for transactions where it is customary.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339#2/r4] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · الجمهور | reports | The majority treat writing debts and witnessing sales or debts as recommended, so the command remains operative without abrogation.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339#2/r5] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن عمر | reports | A group including Ibn ʿUmar, Abu Musa, Mujahid, Ibn Sirin, and others regard writing and witnessing as obligatory.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339#2/r6] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | reports | Among those who require it, most say the ruling remains, while others say it was abrogated by the trust verse at 2:283. | mentions 2:283
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · قتادة | reports | Qatada says the verse followed an incident where a man called around a large tented gathering for witnesses and no one came.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339/r2] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿAtiyya, Qatada, and al-Rabiʿ say witnesses are called to bear testimony and have it recorded.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339/r3] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · سعيد بن جبير | reports | Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Tawus, Mujahid, and others say the call is to perform testimony before judges after first bearing it.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339/r4] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن عباس | reports | A third view, reported from Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Hasan and preferred by al-Zajjaj, includes both bearing and performing testimony.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339/r5] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · القاضي أبو يعلى | holds | Qadi Abu Yaʿla says a witness must attend to perform testimony only if no one else can testify; both bearing and performing it are communal duties like jihad.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p340/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | reports | Abu Jaʿfar reads yuḍār with a light ra and sukun.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p340/r2] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, ʿIkrima, al-Suddi, al-Rabiʿ, al-Farra, and Muqatil say a scribe or witness must not be burdened with a summons while busy; al-Rabiʿ describes a requester insisting despite an available alternative.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p340/r3] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · الحسن | reports | Al-Hasan, Tawus, Qatada, and Ibn Zayd say the scribe must not alter what was dictated, nor the witness testify to something he was not asked to witness; Ibn Qutayba and al-Zajjaj prefer this reading.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p340/r4] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · الزجاج | prefers | Al-Zajjaj argues that falsifying a document or testimony is the sort of harm called transgression in the next clause; merely summoning a busy person would not make one sinful.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p340/r5] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · عطاء | reports | A third view from ʿAta and others says the harm is the scribe refusing to write or the witness refusing to testify.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p341/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | “If you do so” refers to committing this harm.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p100#2/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · الزجاج | reports | Al-Zajjaj reads the command as covering both accepting testimony beforehand and giving it afterward.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p100#2/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | prefers | Al-Razi favors testimony performance: the witnesses are already called witnesses, and the command is obligatory for all, whereas accepting testimony is not required of everyone.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p100#2/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Accepting testimony is already included in the command to appoint two witnesses, so reading the later command as performance gives it a distinct legal function; concealing testimony is separately forbidden. | mentions 2:283
[RAZI-FULL:v7p100#2/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | If the witness is uniquely available, giving testimony is an individual duty; if many can testify, it is a communal duty.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p100#2/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · الشافعي | reports | Al-Shafiʿi permits judgment on one witness plus the claimant’s oath, citing the Prophet’s pr

actice; Abu Hanifa rejects it because the verse specifies two men or one man and two women.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p100#2/r6] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The verse repeats the writing instruction after commanding it earlier as reinforcement of the documentation rule.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p100/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Ḍalāl in the clause can mean forgetting, as in the verse about what vanished from people, or failing to find one’s way; Abu ʿAmr says its root sense is disappearance.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p100/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · نافع وابن عامر وعاصم والكسائي | reports | Nafiʿ, Ibn ʿAmir, ʿAsim, and al-Kisaʾi read فتذكر with doubling and the subjunctive; Hamza doubles it with the indicative, while Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr use the lighter form.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p100/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · سفيان بن عيينة | reports | Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna interprets the second woman as making the first a male-equivalent witness, rather than reminding her of forgotten testimony.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p100/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | rejects | Al-Razi rejects that interpretation as contrary to the general exegetical view: without a man, women’s testimony is not accepted, so the second woman does not simply make the first a witness.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p100/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · أبو عمرو بن العلاء | reports | Abu ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlaʾ also transmits the male-equivalent reading, explaining that the second woman’s testimony joins the first to make one man’s testimony.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p100/r6] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | prefers | Al-Razi says the sounder reading of the phrase forbidding witnesses to refuse is a ban on withholding testimony when the rights-holder needs it.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p100/r7] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · قتادة والقفال | reports | Qatada and al-Qaffal instead understand the command as requiring a person to accept the burden of witnessing, so rights are not lost through lack of records or witnesses.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p101/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Saʾāma means weariness or irritation; the instruction encourages writing small and large debts because even a small dispute can grow into serious conflict.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p101/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The command does not conventionally extend to trivial amounts such as a grain or qirat, since such things are not normally written down.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p101/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The accusative أن can be construed with the following verb as a verbal noun or with an omitted preposition meaning from writing it until its term.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p101/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The pronoun in أن تكتبوه must refer back to either the debt or the right mentioned earlier.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p101/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | A variant reading has ياء in both instances of ولا.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p101/r6] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Al-Qaffal takes ذالكم as referring to the commanded writing and witnessing; writing is more just because it is closer to certainty and truth and further from ignorance and falsehood. | mentions 60:8, 49:9, 33:5
[RAZI-FULL:v7p101/r7] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Qist is justice and iqsat its verbal noun; the related forms mean acting justly or acting unjustly, as illustrated by other Qur’anic passages. | mentions 60:8, 49:9, 72:15
[RAZI-FULL:v7p102#2/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | An takuna may use kāna for occurrence, or incomplete kāna with تجارة حاضرة as its subject and تديرونها as predicate; al-Farraʾ gives the latter parse.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p102#2/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · عاصم | reports | ʿAsim reads تجارة in the accusative, while the other readers use the nominative.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p102#2/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · الزجاج | reports | Al-Zajjaj parses the accusative by supplying مداينة as the subject, while Abu ʿAli al-Farisi objects that a debt transaction cannot be immediate trade.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p102#2/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Al-Razi answers that a sale payable within an hour can still be called immediate commerce despite creating a debt.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p102#2/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Commerce means dealing in property for profit, while تديرونها means exchanging directly hand to hand; the exemption removes hardship rather than declaring that omission is sinful.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p102/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Aqwam means more upright; writing supports accurate testimony through preservation and memory, serving worldly benefit, while the first benefit serves religion and is placed first to prioritize religion.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p102/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Writing also reduces doubt and protects both parties from uncertain recollection and accusations that can lead to backbiting or slander.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p102/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | The exception for immediate trade may be connected to the debt-writing command or to the writer’s duty, or disconnected as a separate concession; ease and immediate exchange explain the concession.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p102/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The exception is justified by the frequency of everyday cash exchanges and the absence of denial risk when both parties exchange their due in the same sitting.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p103/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · أكثر المفسرين | reports | Most exegetes say immediate trade is exempt from writing but remains subject to witnessing, which is easier and avoids later memory failure.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p103/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The commands to record and witness are guidance toward prudent protection of rights.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p103/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · أكثر المفسرين والحسن وطاوس وقتادة | reports | Most exegetes, al-Hasan, Tawus, and Qatada read ولا يضار as forbidding the writer or witness from harming the rights-holder through falsification, omission, or ineffective testimony.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p103/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · ابن مسعود وعطاء ومجاهد | reports | Ibn Masʿud, ʿAtaʾ, and Mujahid instead understand the clause as forbidding the rights-holder from burdening or obstructing the writer and witness.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p103/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · عمر وابن عباس | reports | The ambiguity comes from assimilation in يضارر: the subject may inflict harm or suffer it; Umar’s kasra and Ibn ʿAbbas’s fatḥa with explicit pronunciation preserve both readings. | mentions 2:233
[RAZI-FULL:v7p103/r6] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · الزجاج | prefers | Al-Zajjaj prefers the reading that writers and witnesses must not harm the claimant, while the opposing reading points to the plural address and the ensuing plural verb. | mentions 2:283
[RAZI-FULL:v7p104/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports |  فسوق بكم may refer specifically to committing the prohibited harm, or generally to doing anything forbidden or omitting any commanded duty.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p104/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The call to fear God may likewise refer narrowly to avoiding harm in this transaction or broadly to all commands and prohibitions.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p104/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | God teaches people guidance and safeguards for worldly dealings as well as religious guidance; His knowledge encompasses the interests of both lives.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p92/r6] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Razi identifies the debt-document verse as the third legal ruling discussed in this passage of the surah.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p93#2/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The detailed debt-recording rule follows commands to give charity, avoid usury, and remain mindful of God: preserving lawful wealth enables those duties and protects worldly and religious interests. | mentions 4:5
[RAZI-FULL:v7p93#2/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · القفال | reports | Al-Qaffal sees the verse’s unusually repeated instructions as deliberate emphasis: careful documentation preserves lawful wealth needed for charity and avoidance of forbidden gain.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p94/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · قوم من المفسرين | reports | Some exegetes take the debt transaction here as salam, which provides the benefits sought through usury by a lawful route; the author approves this as a second coherent link.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p94/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | A second account of the passage’s arrangement says the ban on usury is followed by permission for salam, which offers the same desired benefits through lawful means.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p94/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · أهل اللغة | reports | The commentators distinguish a loan, which they say cannot stipulate a term, from a debt sale whose payment may be deferred; the verse’s specified term therefore points beyond a loan.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p94/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · الأحمر | reports | Al-Ahmar cites a line using dāna for borrowing and repayment to illustrate the verb’s debt-related meanings.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p94/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbas says the verse was revealed about forward sales: people in Medina prepaid for dates two or three years ahead, and the Prophet required known measure, weight, and term.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p94/r6] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | rejects | Al-Razi rejects interpreting the debt as a loan because he says a loan cannot stipulate the deferred term specified in the verse.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p94/r7] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · أكثر المفسرين | reports | Most exegetes include both a sale of present goods for deferred payment and salam, while excluding cash-for-cash and debt-for-debt exchanges.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p95#2/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | An appointed term is a future time at which the period ends; its root conveys delay, and a specified debt term must be objectively known, such as by year, month, or days.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p95#2/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Terms such as harvest, threshing, or the pilgrims’ arrival are invalid because they do not specify a determinate date.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p95#2/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Writing and witnesses protect both sides when payment is deferred: the creditor avoids premature or excessive demands, and the debtor avoids denial and can prepare p

[RAZI-FULL:v7p95#2/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · عطاء وابن جريج والنخعي والطبري | reports | ʿAtaʾ, Ibn Jurayj, al-Nakhaʿi, and al-Tabari hold that writing and witnessing deferred debts are obligatory; al-Nakhaʿi even requires witnessing a tiny vegetable purchase.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p95#2/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · جمهور الفقهاء المجتهدين | reports | Most jurists treat the commands as recommendations, citing Muslims’ customary deferred sales without records and the hardship obligatory documentation would cause.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p95#2/r6] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · الحسن والشعبي والحكم وابن عيينة | reports | A group says documentation was once obligatory and was abrogated by the permission to rely on mutual trust in the following verse; al-Razi later rejects abrogation without proof. | mentions 2:283
[RAZI-FULL:v7p95/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Although reciprocal form tadāyantum might suggest each party incurs a debt, al-Razi reads it broadly as transacting in a way that results in a debt.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p95/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · ابن الأنباري | reports | Ibn al-Anbari says bidayn specifies the financial sense of tadāyantum, since the verb can also mean reciprocal recompense.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p95/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · صاحب الكشاف | reports | The author of al-Kashshaf explains that bidayn supplies the antecedent for the pronoun in فاكتبوه and improves the sentence’s ordering.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p95/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | The word bidayn may be emphatic, as in the Qur’anic phrases فسجد الملائكة كلهم أجمعون and ولا طائر يطير بجناحيه. | mentions 15:30, 6:38
[RAZI-FULL:v7p95/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Bidayn can also generalize the rule to small or large transactions and to loans, salam, or deferred sales.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p95/r6] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | prefers | Al-Razi’s own explanation is that adding bidayn limits the reciprocal form to transactions producing one debt, thereby excluding invalid debt-for-debt exchange.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p95/r7] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Although idha alone does not express universal scope, the stated rationale applies to every debt transaction: documentation prevents mistaken claims of increase or loss.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p96/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The command to write does not require every person to write; it requires that the record be made by someone, as the command to cut a thief’s hand is fulfilled by an authorized agent. | mentions 5:38
[RAZI-FULL:v7p96/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | A just record must neither inflate nor reduce the debt and must protect either party’s claim when needed.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p96/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · بعض الفقهاء | reports | Some jurists define justice in drafting as balanced protection for both disputants, agreement with recognized scholarly positions, and avoidance of ambiguous wording that invites dispute.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p96/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Meeting those standards requires a writer skilled in jurisprudence and in distinguishing similar expressions.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p96/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | One reading treats the ban on a writer’s refusal as guidance: writing for another Muslim is gratitude for God’s gift of literacy and legal knowledge. | mentions 28:77
[RAZI-FULL:v7p97/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · الشعبي | reports | Al-Shaʿbi regards writing as a communal obligation: one writer must act if no others are available, while one among several suffices.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p97/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | Another view says the writer’s duty was obligatory but later abrogated by the prohibition on harming writers and witnesses. | mentions 2:282
[RAZI-FULL:v7p97/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | A further interpretation makes the duty conditional: whoever writes must follow God’s taught rules and preserve every safeguard for the parties.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p97/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · الزجاج | reports | Al-Zajjaj gives two grammatical attachments for كما علمه الله: it can complete the preceding ban on refusal or introduce the following command to write.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p97/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The debtor must dictate an acknowledgment of the amount, kind, description, and due date so that the written contract is complete.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p97/r6] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · الفراء | reports | Al-Farraʾ notes that amlal and amla are dialectal alternatives: the first is associated with Hijaz and Banu Asad, the second with Tamim and Qays. | mentions 25:5
[RAZI-FULL:v7p98#2/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | Min rijalikum is variously read as men of the Muslim community, free men, or men considered fit to testify because of justice.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p98#2/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · شريح وابن سيرين وأحمد | reports | Shurayh, Ibn Sirin, and Ahmad accept an enslaved man’s testimony, arguing that the verse is general and that intellect, religion, and justice—not legal status—prevent lying.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p98#2/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · الشافعي وأبو حنيفة | reports | Al-Shafiʿi and Abu Hanifa reject an enslaved person as a witness, reasoning that the command to attend testimony cannot be obligatory for slaves.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p98#2/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | prefers | Al-Razi calls the argument against slave testimony strong, while noting that the general wording can be restricted to people already recognized as qualified witnesses.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p98#2/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · علي بن عيسى | reports | Ali ibn ʿIsa gives four permissible implied predicates for the nominative phrase رجل وامرأتان, including let there be, let testify, or the witnesses are.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p98/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The debtor must dictate without diminishing any amount owed; if the debtor is not competent to make a valid acknowledgment, the guardian’s acknowledgment counts.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p98/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The conjunction أو marks three distinct conditions: an adult with deficient judgment, someone lacking capacity such as a child or incapacitated elder, and someone unable to dictate because of speech or knowledge limitations.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p98/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | For each of those three classes, the relevant guardian dictates fairly; the guardian of an incapacitated person can acknowledge debts as in the person’s other affairs.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p98/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · ابن عباس ومقاتل والربيع | rejects | Ibn ʿAbbas, Muqatil, and al-Rabiʿ say the wali is the creditor, but al-Razi rejects this because a claimant’s assertion alone would make documentation and witnesses pointless.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p98/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The purpose of witnesses is to let the creditor establish the claim if the debtor later denies it; istashhidu means make someone testify, and shahidayn means two witnesses.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p99/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The qualification ممن ترضون and the parallel divorce instruction show that not everyone may testify; jurists enumerate ten conditions, including freedom, adulthood, Islam, justice, knowledge, and lack of personal conflict or benefit. | mentions 65:2
[RAZI-FULL:v7p99/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Al-Razi explains the two-women provision by saying a second woman can prompt the first if she forgets, which he attributes to women’s bodily temperament.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p99/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · حمزة | reports | Hamza reads إن with kasra and فتذكر as a raised, doubled form, taking the construction as conditional; the jussive of تضل is obscured by its doubled consonant.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p99/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · سائر القراء | reports | Other readers use accusative أن, parsed either as لأن تضل with an elided preposition or as a purpose clause.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p99/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Al-Razi answers the objection that testimony aims at remembrance by saying the wording serves both reliable testimony and the stated comparative legal treatment of men and women.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · مالك | reports | He accepts the pledgee's sworn account only up to the collateral's value, treating the pledge and oath as supporting him; al-Qurṭubī says the verse instead favors the debtor, and collateral value need not match the debt.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | If وليّه means guardian, the verse implies that a guardian's acknowledgment is valid for the orphan under his care.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | A transaction by an interdicted fool without the guardian's permission is invalid by consensus; an unimpaired but foolish person who has not been interdicted is discussed under Sūrat al-Nisāʾ.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | prefers | Seeking witnesses is recommended, not obligatory, as al-Qurṭubī explains later.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | God generally requires two witnesses for financial and bodily claims and legal penalties, except adultery; شهيد is an intensive form suggesting repeated testimony and thus justice.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · مجاهد | reports | He says رجالكم means free men; Shurayh, Uthman al-Batti, Ahmad, Ishaq, and Abu Thawr accept an upright slave's testimony, unlike Malik, Abu Hanifa, al-Shafiʿi, and the majority; al-Qurṭubī prefers the majority, while al-Shaʿbi and al-Nakhaʿi permit slaves' testimony in minor matters.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | prefers | He rejects slave testimony because the address concerns transacting believers, while slaves do not own such assets independently; he also invokes the later restriction on witnesses refusing a summons.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r8] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن عباس | reports | He transmits the Prophet's instruction that a witness should testify only to what is as clear as seeing the sun, establishing direct certainty rather than inference.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#11/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671
<<part 31 ends; continues in part 32>>

<<2:282 notes, part 32 of 0..65>>
 · author | holds | Witnesses must directly know what they attest: probable inference may suffice for ordinary acts such as accepting a gift or recognizing a spouse by voice, but not testimony about another's admission, sale, slander, or seizure.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#11/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الشافعي وابن أبي ليلى وأبو يوسف | reports | They accept testimony after blindness when the witness already knew the person before losing sight, analogizing the impairment to absence or death; al-Qurṭubī sees no reason to reject testimony previously borne while sighted and accepts public knowledge for lineage.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#11/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | rejects | Some accept a blind person's voice-based testimony as certain, but al-Qurṭubī rejects this because it would imply that a sighted person could likewise rely on sound alone.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#11/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · مالك | reports | Malik permits an established voice-based testimony by a blind person, including on divorce; Ibn Qasim reports him accepting testimony from a man who heard his neighbor divorce through a wall, with several early jurists sharing the view.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#11/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الجمهور | prefers | If two male witnesses are not produced, the claimant should bring one man and two women; the male noun is nominative and the women coordinated, with the predicate omitted to mean they take the two men's place.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#11/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · قول | reports | Another parsing says the female witnesses may be used only when no men can be found; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls this weak because the verse's apparent sense allows one man and two women even when two men are available.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#11/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الجمهور | holds | The one-man-and-two-women arrangement applies to financial matters and requires a man, since financial transactions are common and have multiple safeguards: writing, witnesses, collateral, and guarantees.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The debt-transactions clause does not encompass testimony about a marriage dowry or settlement for intentional homicide, because those testimonies concern marriage rather than debt.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Women may testify alone in matters that no one else can observe, out of necessity.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · مالك | reports | Malik permits children's testimony in injuries among children if they have not disagreed or separated; at least two are required, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr also judged by it, which Malik calls established practice.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الشافعي وأبو حنيفة وأصحابه | reports | They reject children's testimony because children lack the qualifications of men, approved witnesses, and just adults named elsewhere in scripture. | mentions 5:95
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Because two women replace one man, he reasons by analogy that their testimony can be accompanied by an oath just as one man's testimony can; al-Shafiʿi agrees, while Abu Hanifa and his companions reject the oath as an extra division beyond the text.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الثوري والأوزاعي وعطاء والحكم بن عتيبة وطائفة | reports | They oppose judgment by an oath with a witness; some call that practice abrogated by the Quran, and ʿAṭāʾ alleges ʿAbd al-Malik first ruled that way while al-Ḥakam attributes it to Muʿāwiya.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | rejects | Al-Qurṭubī calls those accusations mistaken: the verse does not negate the Prophet's ruling by an oath and one witness, and an exclusive reading would also invalidate claims proved when a defendant refuses to swear, contrary to consensus.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r8] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · مالك | reports | He argues that when a defendant denies a claim and refuses the oath, the claimant may swear and establish it; because this accepted procedure is absent from the Quran's witness list, its existence proves the list is not exhaustive and supports the oath with one witness.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#13/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | rejects | Al-Qurṭubī rebukes those who reject judgment by an oath and one witness despite sound reports and early authorities' practice.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#13/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن عباس | reports | The Prophet ruled by an oath together with one witness; ʿAmr ibn Dīnār restricts the report to property cases.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#13/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · أبو عمرو | reports | Abū ʿAmr calls the report's chain the soundest and its transmitters trustworthy, citing Muslim and other critics.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#13/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الزهري | reports | One report from al-Zuhrī calls judgment by oath and witness an innovation and insists on two witnesses; another says he first ruled by it.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#13/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | prefers | Al-Qurṭubī endorses the majority position allowing an oath with one witness, based on transmitted reports and generations of Medinan practice; Mālik allowed it in every region.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#13/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · يحيى بن يحيى | reports | In al-Andalus, Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā said he had not seen al-Layth issue a ruling or hold the doctrine, thereby opposing Mālik and Medinan practice.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Prophetic Sunnah may add rulings to the Qurʾān, as in prohibited marriage combinations, foods, and wiping over footwear alongside Qurʾānic wording. | mentions 4:24, 6:145, 9:92
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r10] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · المهدوي | reports | Al-Mahdawī says most jurists reject women's testimony in criminal penalties, marriage, and divorce, and do not let them transmit testimony where they cannot testify directly.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | rejects | The Qurʾān's general permission for sales cannot abrogate the Prophet's bans on uncertain and nonexistent sales; Sunnah explains scripture. | mentions 2:275, 4:29
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | rejects | Although one might call the oath-and-witness ruling case-specific, al-Qurṭubī reads it as establishing a general legal rule.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · أبو داود | reports | A report of Ibn ʿAbbās transmitted by Abū Dāwūd expressly says the Prophet judged by one witness and an oath in rights cases.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | By analogy, an oath has stronger evidentiary standing than two women because women have no role in mutual imprecation, whereas an oath does.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Once sound Sunnah is established, it must be followed and needs no supporting precedent; those who oppose it are answered by it.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · القاضي أبو محمد عبد الوهاب | reports | Among jurists accepting oath-plus-witness, its use is limited by consensus to property and related rights, not bodily rights; property rights are lower because women's testimony is accepted there.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r8] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | prefers | Mālik has two reports about intentional injury: one allows a choice between retaliation and compensation, while the sounder report allows neither because bodily rights are involved.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r9] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · المازري | reports | Al-Māzarī reports agreement on oath-plus-witness for pure money claims and rejection for marriage or divorce as such; claims leading only to money are disputed.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Mālik's school accepts two women's testimony in matters unavailable to other witnesses, such as childbirth and a newborn's first cry, though details are disputed.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r10] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Because testimony is a grave authority that makes another person liable, God requires approved and upright witnesses with distinguishing qualities.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن بكير | reports | Ibn Bukayr and others take the address requiring approved witnesses to be directed to judges.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن عطية | rejects | Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects limiting the address to judges: it addresses everyone, although judges carry out the case in practice.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · جمهور | reports | The majority infer that probity is an additional qualification beyond being Muslim, since the verse requires witnesses whom people approve.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · أبو حنيفة | reports | Abū Ḥanīfa regards any apparently Muslim person free of manifest wrongdoing as upright, even when character is unknown.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · شريح وعثمان البتى وأبو ثور | reports | Shurayḥ, ʿUthmān al-Battī, and Abū Thawr count Muslims as upright witnesses even if enslaved.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | prefers | A Bedouin may testify for a town-dweller if upright: Qurʾānic general wording does not distinguish them, and al-Qurṭubī rejects a restrictive report. | mentions 65:2
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r8] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · مالك وأحمد بن حنبل | reports | Mālik in one report and Aḥmad reject a Bedouin's testimony for a town-dweller, relying on a report from Abū Hurayra.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r9] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · علماؤنا | reports | Probity means religious steadiness: avoiding major sins, preserving respectable conduct and avoiding minor sins, while appearing trustworthy and alert; another definition stresses apparent integrity.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#16/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The requirement of witness approval supports inference from signs and entrusts judges with discretion to detect carelessness or suspicion and
