 reject testimony.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#16/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · أبو حنيفة | reports | Abū Ḥanīfa accepts apparent Muslim status as enough in property cases but not criminal penalties.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#16/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن العربي | reports | Ibn al-ʿArabī calls that distinction self-defeating: a property claim is a right and should not receive weaker witness scrutiny than a criminal penalty.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#16/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | rejects | Upright witnesses are even more important for marriage than debt, given its effects on lawful status, punishment, and lineage; al-Qurṭubī rejects Abū Ḥanīfa's view. | mentions 2:204, 63:4
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#16/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Apparent profession of Islam does not establish probity, since impressive speech or appearance may conceal disqualifying conduct. | mentions 2:204, 63:4
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#16/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · أبو عبيد | reports | Abū ʿUbayd glosses the verb for straying as forgetting; in testimony, a witness may recall one part while forgetting another and become uncertain.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#16/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · حمزة | reports | Ḥamza reads the particle with kasra as a conditional; the following clause answers it and the phrase describes the witnesses. | mentions 5:95
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#17/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · سيبويه | reports | Under Ḥamza's conditional reading, Sībawayh parses the following verb as a new clause; with the open particle it is an object of purpose with an omitted governor.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#17/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · النحاس | reports | Al-Naḥḥās allows several vocalizations of the verb, including forms reflecting the dialect that says ḍalaltu taḍillu.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#17/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الجحدري وعيسى بن عمر | reports | Al-Jaḥdarī and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read the verb with a pattern meaning that one forgets.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#17/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · النقاش | reports | Al-Naqqāsh reports another al-Jaḥdarī reading, with the testimony itself going astray or being lost.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#17/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · سفيان بن عيينة وأبو عمرو بن العلاء | reports | Ibn ʿUyayna and Abū ʿAmr understand the lighter reading of the reminder verb as returning a woman's testimony to memory, so two women's testimony totals a man's.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#18/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | prefers | Al-Qurṭubī finds the lighter reminder reading less apt: a reminder naturally answers forgetfulness, and the doubled reading means one woman alerts the other when she forgets.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#18/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الحسن | reports | Al-Ḥasan says the command not to refuse witnesses covers both being asked to record testimony and to deliver testimony already held.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#18/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · قتادة والربيع وابن عباس | reports | Qatāda, al-Rabīʿ, and Ibn ʿAbbās interpret the summons as a request to bear witness and enter it in writing.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#18/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · مجاهد | reports | Mujāhid interprets the summons as a request to give testimony already held; he and others say an initial invitation to witness may be declined.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#18/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن عطية | reports | Ibn ʿAṭiyya treats assistance as recommended when witnesses are plentiful, increasingly urgent when rights may be lost, and obligatory when delay will destroy a right.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#18/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Al-Qurṭubī infers that a ruler may employ public witnesses and support them from the treasury to preserve people's rights; this is public support like judges' salaries, not a fee. | mentions 9:60
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#19/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The verse indicates that witnesses go to the judge when summoned, a practice established across legal traditions and reflected in a proverb.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#19/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | An enslaved person is excluded from the witness class because he cannot independently answer a summons, just as he lacks independent authority in other duties.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#19/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | rejects | Al-Qurṭubī rejects the view that testimony already held is merely recommended: it is obligatory when a right risks loss, supported by Qurʾānic commands and the Prophet's call to aid the wronged. | mentions 65:2, 43:86
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#19/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن القاسم | reports | Ibn al-Qāsim and others say refusing a required testimony damages the witness and testimony generally, whether the right belongs to God or a person.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#19/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | prefers | Al-Qurṭubī prefers general disqualification: wrongful refusal is misconduct that removes eligibility for testimony altogether.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Salam is a sale of a specified, described commodity in liability for present capital or its equivalent, due at a known term.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Requiring liability excludes unknown goods and specified individual orchards whose fruit may fail; full description excludes unspecified kinds or qualities of dates, cloth, or fish.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Present capital excludes debt-for-debt; treating it as present permits a two- or three-day delay in paying salam capital, which Malik allows, while al-Shafiʿi and Kufans forbid any delay after contract and separation by analogy with currency exchange.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Al-Qurṭubī distinguishes salam from currency exchange: exchange has many strict conditions, while salam more closely resembles ordinary transactions and tolerates more flexibility.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | A known term excludes spot salam, which is impermissible on the commonly held view, and excludes the pre-Islamic unknown terms.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Salam and salaf refer to the same transaction, but salam is its specific name because salaf can also mean a loan; salam is a unanimously permitted sale excepted from the ban on selling what one does not possess.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Salam is licensed to meet mutual needs: the buyer needs the harvest and the grower needs money before it ripens; it is a sale for the needy, and an immediate sale would defeat that purpose.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r8] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The agreed conditions are six for the goods—liability, description, measurement, deferral, known term, and availability at maturity—and three for capital—known kind, specified measure, and cash payment, with cash status disputed.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r9] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن العربي | reports | He says the first requirement, liability, is self-evident because salam is a debt transaction sought for benefit and accommodation.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#20/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Praise of witnesses who volunteer testimony does not conflict with a report condemning people who testify without being asked; the latter has three possible readings.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#20/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · أبو بكر بن أبي شيبة | reports | Ibn Abī Shayba reports that ʿUmar warned of later false testimony, distinguishing corrupt witnesses from truthful help preserving rights.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#20/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | reports | One interpretation is that greed or bias makes a person eagerly present testimony before being asked; Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī reports that boys were warned against contracts and testimony.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#20/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الأخفش | reports | Al-Akhfash explains the verb for becoming weary as boredom and gives its verbal nouns; an unnamed poet illustrates weariness after eighty years of life.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#21/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The writing phrase is accusative after the verb, and small or large are circumstantial descriptions; small comes first for emphasis, since people might neglect tiny debts.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#21/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · علماؤنا | reports | The jurists except a tiny amount such as a qirat because people do not normally care to affirm or deny it.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#21/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The verse's terms mean fairest, soundest and most protective for testimony, closer, and that people should not doubt.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#21/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن المنذر | reports | Ibn al-Mundhir says most scholars reject testimony based solely on handwriting when the witness no longer remembers; Mālik argues from Joseph's report. | mentions 12:81
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#21/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن المبارك | reports | Ibn al-Mubārak approves the report that a witness may testify from a document bearing his mark or handwriting even if he forgot the testimony.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#21/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Reports of the Prophet's judgments and earlier prophets support accepting reliable signs and indications as evidence.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الأخفش أبو سعيد | reports | Al-Akhfash explains the exception as a sale that occurs immediately; other grammarians parse its predicate differently, while ʿĀṣim reads an implicit subject.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | God lifts writing requirements for cash exchanges, commonly small purchases, because writing them would be burdensome; al-Suddī and al-Ḍaḥḥāk specify hand-to-hand sales.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Immediate reciprocal possession reduces disputes, while real estate and animals are less readily transferred or hidden; deferred transactions need written safeguards against changed circumstances and distrust.

2:282#22/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الشافعي | reports | Al-Shāfiʿī classifies sales as documented with witnesses, secured by a pledge, or based on trust, reading the verse as evidence for these forms.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن عمر | reports | Ibn ʿUmar would obtain witnesses for cash sales and write down deferred sales.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الطبري | reports | Al-Ṭabarī reads the witnessing command as covering small and large sales; Abū Mūsā, Ibn ʿUmar, and others hold it obligatory, and ʿAṭāʾ demands witnesses for tiny purchases.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الشعبي والحسن | reports | Al-Shaʿbī and al-Ḥasan treat witnessing as recommendation and guidance rather than a binding duty; Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, and other jurists are also said to hold this.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r8] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن العربي | prefers | Ibn al-ʿArabī says the recommendation is the view of all jurists and is correct.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#23/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن العربي | reports | Ibn al-ʿArabī says only al-Ḍaḥḥāk is reported to require witnessing; the Prophet made and recorded sales without witnesses and pledged his armor without them.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#23/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | rejects | Al-Qurṭubī notes that the obligation was attributed to several authorities besides al-Ḍaḥḥāk, correcting Ibn al-ʿArabī's account.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#23/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن عطية | reports | Ibn ʿAṭiyya finds mandatory witnessing impractical for small sales and sometimes socially awkward; he treats it as recommended for its usual benefit unless an excuse intervenes.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#23/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · النحاس | reports | Al-Ḥasan, al-Ḥakam, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd are reported to say that the mutual-trust clause abrogated witnessing sales. | mentions 2:283
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#23/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الطبري | rejects | Al-Ṭabarī rejects abrogation: the pledge clause addresses inability to find a scribe and an unrequired pledge, a different case from writing and witnessing. | mentions 2:283, 4:43, 5:6
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#24/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | rejects | Later rules for different situations do not abrogate earlier rules; some note both clauses may have been revealed together, since abrogation cannot occur simultaneously. | mentions 5:6, 4:92, 58:4
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#24/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās says the debt verse is established, not abrogated, and writing, pledges, and witnesses are alternative means of securing debt; witnessing is recommended like pledging. | mentions 2:283
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#24/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | prefers | Al-Qurṭubī says explicit Sunnah showing the Prophet accepted a sale without witnesses is an even stronger argument against mandatory witnessing.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#24/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · طارق بن عبد الله المحاربي | reports | Ṭāriq ibn ʿAbd Allāh recounts selling a camel to a man later identified as the Prophet; the Prophet sent word for the sellers to take dates and eat until satisfied, without witnesses at the sale.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#25/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · عمارة بن خزيمة | reports | ʿUmāra ibn Khuzayma reports that his Companion uncle witnessed the Prophet's purchase of a horse from a Bedouin, and Khuzayma ibn Thābit testified from trust in the Prophet.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#25/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · خزيمة بن ثابت | reports | The Prophet made Khuzayma's testimony count as that of two men because he testified on the basis of believing the Prophet.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#25/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الحسن وقتادة وطاوس وابن زيد | reports | Al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, Ṭāwūs, and Ibn Zayd say a scribe must write only what is dictated and a witness must neither add to nor subtract from testimony.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#25/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن عباس ومجاهد وعطاء | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and ʿAṭāʾ interpret the prohibition as forbidding a scribe or witness from refusing when asked to serve.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#26/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · النحاس | reports | Al-Naḥḥās reports Abū Isḥāq's preference for the reading that forbids falsifying a record or testimony, since the warning of sin fits dishonesty better than burdening a busy witness.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#26/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · مجاهد والضحاك وطاوس والسدي | reports | Mujāhid, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Ṭāwūs, and al-Suddī understand the verse to forbid harassing a busy scribe or witness who gives a reasonable excuse; Ibn Masʿūd has a similar reading.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#26/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The reciprocal form encompasses both kinds of harm: dishonest additions and omissions wrongfully affect people and property, while imposing on busy witnesses violates God's command.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#26/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · سفيان الثوري | reports | Sufyān al-Thawrī explains 'it is wrongdoing by you' as meaning a sinful act; falsifying testimony and imposing on busy witnesses are both disobedience.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#26/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | God promises that reverent people receive understanding and discernment to distinguish truth from falsehood, sometimes placed directly in the heart. | mentions 8:29
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#27/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The promise that piety gives believers discernment is linked to the verse promising a criterion by which to distinguish right from wrong. | mentions 8:29
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#3/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · مالك | reports | He alone allows salam in a designated item under two conditions: it comes from a secure village, and collection has begun, as with milk from a sheep or ripe fruit from a palm.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#3/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | prefers | He accepts Malik's exceptions: a secure location makes non-delivery unlikely enough to tolerate slight uncertainty, and daily collection of milk or dates meets a recurring need when buyers lack cash or prices fluctuate and sellers need money.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#4/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The Prophetic wording إلى أجل معلوم settles the requirement for a known term; al-Qurṭubī allows one to three days when prices differ between towns, but not within one town where the price is stable.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#4/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | There is consensus that the term must be known; Malik alone also accepts harvest or fruit-picking as a sufficiently known deadline, discussed under the verse about lunar phases. | mentions 2:189
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#4/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | There is consensus that the goods must exist at maturity; if they fail to exist then through God's decree, the contract is dissolved according to all scholars.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#4/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The seller need not own the goods throughout the contract; reports from Ibn Abi Awfa and Ibn Abza say the Companions did not ask Syrian sellers whether they farmed the grain or oil they promised.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#4/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · أبو حنيفة | reports | He requires the goods to exist continuously from contract through maturity, fearing that the promised goods may be unavailable when demanded; other jurists require existence only at maturity.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#4/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الكوفيون والثوري | reports | They require the delivery location for goods involving transport and invalidate salam if it is omitted; al-Awzāʿī calls omission disliked.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#4/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | prefers | If the place is unstated, the contract remains valid and delivery defaults to the contract location, as held by Ahmad, Ishaq, and hadith scholars; the Ibn ʿAbbās report omits the place, although it specifies measure, weight, and term.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · أبو سعيد الخدري | reports | A report through ʿAṭiyya says the Prophet forbade redirecting an advance-purchase contract to a different commodity; ʿAbd al-Ḥaqq says the transmitter al-ʿAwfī is not an authority, despite prominent scholars transmitting from him.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r10] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الجمهور | prefers | The majority treat documentation as recommended protection against lost property and doubt; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls this correct because a person may waive a financial claim, so there is no abrogation.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r11] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · عطاء وغيره | reports | They say the writer must write when asked if no other writer is available; al-Shaʿbī gives the same ruling.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · مالك | reports | If a salam seller cannot deliver at maturity and the buyer releases him, the buyer may take only the original currency or exact capital; exchanging it for another good before receipt would sell food before possession, which the Prophet forbade.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | فاكتبوه commands recording the debt and its term; some say it also implies witnesses, since writing without witnesses is not legal proof, and it prevents forgetting.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن عباس | reports | A report says Adam first denied a written gift: God showed him David among his descendants, allowed forty years of Adam's thousand-year life to be added to David's sixty, recorded and witnessed the gift, then produced the document when Adam denied it; David received a hundred years and Adam completed his thousand.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The command to write calls for recording every detail that identifies the debt, preventing disputes and enabling a judge to decide if the parties later disagree.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الطبري | reports | He holds that documenting every debt, whether sale or loan, is obligatory to prevent forgetfulness or denial.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن جريج |

 reports | He says a lender should write while a seller should obtain witnesses.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r8] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الشعبي | reports | He says people regarded the following clause about mutual trust as abrogating the order to write; Ibn Jurayj, Ibn Zayd, and a report from Abu Saʿid are similar.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r9] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الربيع | reports | He says writing was initially obligatory under these words, then God eased the requirement with the clause permitting trusted transactions.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · السدي | reports | He says the writer must do so when free.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r10] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن العربي | prefers | He says the command is guidance, so the writer need not write before being paid.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r11] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The verb أبى يأبى is an unusual conjugation, grouped with a few other exceptional patterns.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The imperative lam is omitted before a second-person verb but retained with a third-person verb; the text cites 10:58 and a poetic line to illustrate retention and omission. | mentions 10:58
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Writing with justice means accurately recording the claim without adding or subtracting anything.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The impartial writer stands between debtor and creditor because each might suspect the other of biased documentation; alternatively, the command reflects that some people can write and some cannot.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The phrase بالعدل attaches to the act of writing rather than the writer, since a child, slave, or careful layperson could write accurately; appointed notaries must still be upright, knowledgeable, and trusted, as Malik says.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · مالك | reports | He says official document writers must be legally knowledgeable, upright, and trustworthy.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الطبري والربيع | reports | They say the writer is obligated to write when asked.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r8] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الحسن | reports | He makes writing obligatory only where refusal would harm the creditor because no substitute writer is available; otherwise the writer has latitude.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r9] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الربيع والضحاك | reports | They say the order to write was abrogated by the prohibition against harming a writer or witness; al-Qurṭubī calls this remote because a universal obligation was never established and paid document-writing is permitted.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The كاف in كما علمه الله may attach to the command that he write as taught, to the meaning of not refusing because God taught him, or—if the clause ends at أن يكتب—to فليكتب in a new sentence.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The person who owes the debt is the debtor, and must dictate it aloud so his obligation is known.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | إملال and إملاء are two forms: Hijaz and Banu Asad say أمل, Tamim says أملى; the Quran uses both, including 25:5, and the second lām becomes yāʾ for ease. | mentions 25:5
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The debtor dictates because the testimony follows his admission; he must fear God and not diminish the debt, since بَخْس means reduction, as also in 2:228. | mentions 2:228
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · قول | reports | Some say سفيها means a minor, but al-Qurṭubī rejects this because an adult may also be financially foolish.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The verse distinguishes the independent debtor from three who cannot dictate: the fool, the weak-minded, and the person unable to dictate; debts can also arise through inheritance distributions.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | A fool has poor financial judgment and cannot manage giving or receiving; the word is likened to a loosely woven cloth, and can also describe crude speech associated with shallow minds.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r8] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Arabic usage applies سفه to weakness of mind or body, as the cited lines demonstrate for judgment and weakened, swaying spear tops.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | prefers | Some distinguish ḍamma for bodily weakness from fatḥa for weakness of judgment; another view treats both as dialects, but he prefers the distinction.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · أنس بن مالك | reports | He reports that a mentally impaired trader's family asked the Prophet to interdict him; the Prophet stopped him from selling, then allowed him to trade only if he said there was no deception. Al-Tirmidhī calls the report sound.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · البخاري | reports | His historical record gives a related wording requiring the trader to say there is no deception and granting three nights' option on each purchase.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | reports | The trader was Habban ibn Munqidh, though another account calls Munqidh the grandfather of Yahya and Wasiʿ; he lived 130 years and a battle wound to his head impaired his mind and speech.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن عمر | reports | Al-Dāraquṭnī transmits that Habban had poor sight and a head wound, so the Prophet gave him three days' option; his impaired speech rendered لا خلابة as لا خذابة.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | خلابة means deception, as in the proverb that if one cannot overcome someone, one should trick him.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · أحمد وإسحاق | reports | They support interdicting a person who is repeatedly cheated in sales because of inexperience or impaired judgment; other scholars oppose interdiction, and the Maliki school has both views.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r8] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | prefers | He prefers interdiction under this verse and the family's request; the Prophet's concession was specific to Habban because he insisted on trading, while someone ordinarily cheated—especially through mental impairment—should be interdicted.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#9/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · محمد بن إسحاق عن محمد بن يحيى بن حبان | reports | The Prophet told Habban to say لا خلابة when selling and gave him three nights to keep or return each purchase; Habban invoked this right even when mocked by sellers, and Companions confirmed his claim. Al-Dāraquṭnī records it; Abu ʿUmar cites al-Bukhari's historical transmission.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#9/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The weak debtor is someone impaired in reason or nature and unable to dictate because of stammering, muteness, or inability to express himself; his guardian may be a father or trustee.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#9/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The person unable to dictate includes a minor, whose guardian is a trustee or father, and an absent person unable due to illness or another excuse, whose guardian is an agent; a mute could fit either category but fits unable best.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#9/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الطبري | reports | He takes وليه to refer to the debt itself, with reports from al-Rabiʿ and Ibn ʿAbbās; al-Qurṭubī rejects this as unsound and says Ibn ʿAbbās's report is not reliable.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#9/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | prefers | وليّه correctly refers to the debtor; having the creditor dictate a new liability for a fool would not be lawful, though a sick or mute person may hear a creditor's fair dictation and acknowledge it when complete.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#9/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Since the debtor is trusted to dictate, a pledgor's sworn account of the debt prevails while the collateral remains; most jurists and Ibn al-Mundhir agree because the creditor claims the excess, in keeping with the rule that the claimant bears proof and the defendant swears.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · سعيد بن المسيب | reports | He says he was told that the debt verse was the latest Quranic revelation at the Throne.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r10] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Scholars agree valid salam specifies described, commonly available food, measure, term, payment in known currency before the parties separate, and delivery place; he knows no scholar who invalidates such a contract.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r11] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Maliki scholars permit tying salam to harvest, fruit-picking, Nowruz, or Mihrajan because these mark known times.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن عباس | reports | He says the verse was revealed specifically about salam, prompted by the people of Medina, but by consensus it covers all deferred debt transactions.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن خويزمنداد | reports | He says the verse contains thirty legal rulings.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · بعض علمائنا | reports | Some Maliki scholars infer that loans may be deferred because the verse does not distinguish loans from other debt contracts; the Shafiʿis reply that it only orders documentation of an already deferred debt and that term rules come from other evidence.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | بدين is emphatic; a debt is a transaction with one present countervalue and another deferred in liability, since Arabs call what is present عين and what is absent دين. | mentions 6:38, 15:30
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The wording إلى أجل مسمى states the required known, fixed term; two poetic lines use دين for a deferred rather than immediate obligation.

ULL:2:282/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن المنذر | reports | He says إلى أجل مسمى proves salam with an unknown term is invalid, as also shown by Prophetic practice.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r8] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن عباس | reports | He transmits the Prophet's rule for advance purchase of dates: specify measure, weight, and term; al-Qurṭubī says Bukhari, Muslim, and others recorded it.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r9] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن عمر | reports | He says pre-Islamic buyers sold camel meat until the offspring of an offspring was born; the Prophet forbade this indeterminate term.
[QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#8/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | prefers | Malik and one Shafi'i view restore guardianship if a released person becomes wasteful; Abu Hanifa says it cannot return, but al-Qurtubi cites the Quran's protection of wealth and its provision for a guardian when a debtor becomes foolish or weak. | mentions 4:5, 2:282
[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:282#2/r1] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · حمزة | reports | Hamza reads an taḍilla conditionally, with fa-tudhakkira in the indicative.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:282#2/r10] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Doing harm or another prohibited act is disobedience; fear God in violations, and He teaches laws containing people's welfare.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:282#2/r11] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | The repeated name of God in three clauses signals their independence: exhortation to piety, a promise of favor, and magnification greater than a pronoun would provide.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:282#2/r2] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ويعقوب | reports | Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Yaqub read fa-tudhakkira from the form ifkār, to remind.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:282#2/r3] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Witnesses must not refuse to give or undertake testimony; they are called witnesses in advance because the expected event is treated as imminent, and mā is extra.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:282#2/r4] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Do not tire of recording any debt, small or large and brief or detailed, until its agreed due date; that refers to writing.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:282#2/r5] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Writing is more just before God, more reliable for testimony, and likelier to prevent doubt about debt kind, amount, date, and witnesses; aqsaṭ and aqwam have irregular morphological analyses.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:282#2/r6] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | The exception covers present trade managed hand to hand, whether exchanging debt or goods, where writing is less necessary to prevent dispute and forgetfulness.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:282#2/r7] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · عاصم | reports | Asim reads tijāratan in the accusative as a predicate with an omitted subject; the other readers make it nominative, either with tadīrūnahā as predicate or as a complete verb.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:282#2/r8] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Witness the sale in particular or every sale as safer; most imams recommend the commands, while some require them and debate whether they remain effective or are abrogated.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:282#2/r9] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Lā yuḍārr has two readings: scribes and witnesses must not refuse, distort, or alter testimony, or others must not harm them by disrupting duties, demanding extra travel, or withholding their fees and expenses.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:282/r1] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Tadāyantum means dealing with one another on credit as giver or taker; mentioning debt excludes a possible sense of reciprocity, shows deferred and current debts, and explains writing.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:282/r10] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | A guardian dictates for a child or impaired person; an agent or translator does so for someone unable, supporting representation in admissions, perhaps only for matters handled by that representative.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:282/r11] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Witnesses are sought for the debt; men from your community means Muslims, which most scholars require, while Abu Hanifa accepts non-Muslims' testimony among themselves.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:282/r12] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · أبو حنيفة | reports | Abu Hanifa accepts testimony by non-Muslims against one another.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:282/r13] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | If two men are unavailable, one man and two women may testify; the source's school limits this to financial matters, while Abu Hanifa extends it outside fixed penalties and retaliation.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:282/r14] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Witnesses must be people whose uprightness is known; one woman may remind the other if she forgets, with reminder the real rationale and forgetting its trigger.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:282/r15] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | The verse's explanation implies women's lesser reason and memory; it expresses reminder through its cause, like preparing a weapon to repel an enemy if one comes.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:282/r2] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | The specified term is known by days or months, not left to harvest or the pilgrims' arrival; writing is safer and most scholars recommend it.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:282/r3] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas says the verse concerns advance sale, which God allowed when forbidding usury.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:282/r4] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | The writer must be fair and add or subtract nothing; the parties should choose a learned, religious writer so the document is reliable and lawful.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:282/r5] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | A scribe must not refuse; writing as taught by God may mean legal documents or benefiting others with the skill, like the cited command to do good. | mentions 28:77
[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:282/r6] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | The second command to write may emphasize the ban on refusal, or the prohibition may be general while the command specifies the form.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:282/r7] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | The debtor dictates because he acknowledges the claim and is the person testified against; imlāl and imlāʾ mean the same.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:282/r8] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | The command to fear God may address the debtor or scribe; neither may reduce any part of the debt or dictated statement.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:282/r9] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | A deficient debtor may be mentally unsound and profligate, a child or impaired elder, or unable to dictate because mute or ignorant of the language.
[GHARNATI:v1p179/r2] GHARNATI, d. 708 · author | holds | The author invokes the Qurʾan’s exalted standing in the heavenly register as part of his praise of the divine gift of scripture. | mentions 43:4
[GHARNATI:v1p179/r3] GHARNATI, d. 708 · author | holds | Muhammad is praised as the chosen prophet endowed with the Book and clear proofs that open the path for people of insight.
[GHARNATI:v1p179/r4] GHARNATI, d. 708 · author | holds | The cited warning says that only one who follows the Reminder and fears the Merciful unseen benefits from the Messenger’s warning. | mentions 36:11
[GHARNATI:v1p179/r5] GHARNATI, d. 708 · النبي | reports | The Prophet says every prophet received signs sufficient for people to believe, while his own special gift was revelation, through which he hopes to have the most followers on Judgment Day.
[GHARNATI:v1p179/r6] GHARNATI, d. 708 · author | holds | The author says the Prophet had countless miracles besides the Qurʾan, but the Qurʾan is the clearest, wisest, most guiding, and most enduring miracle.
[GHARNATI:v1p179/r7] GHARNATI, d. 708 · author | holds | The Qurʾan joins proof and testimony with clarification of the path and the condition of each group, and remains directly observable to those who reflect.
[GHARNATI:v1p179/r8] GHARNATI, d. 708 · author | holds | Unlike other miracles known through later reports rather than direct observation, the Qurʾan remains pure and present for reflection across the ages.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r1] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | Tadāyantum means dealing with one another by debt, whether one lends or borrows.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r10] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | The debtor must fear God, neither refusing to dictate in denial of the debt nor understating any part of it.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r11] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | reports | Safīh may mean mentally impaired or legally restrained for wastefulness and poor judgment; ḍaʿīf means a child; inability includes stammering, muteness, or not knowing the language.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r12] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | When the debtor cannot dictate, the guardian who manages his affairs dictates truthfully and justly.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r13] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | Two witnesses are sought from believing men; Islam, freedom, and adulthood are conditions, while the author's school accepts non-Muslims testifying among themselves.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r14] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | If two men are unavailable, one man and two women may witness; male testimony with women is accepted outside fixed punishments and retaliation.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r15] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | The witnesses should be people whose uprightness is known; this implies some witnesses are not approved.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r16] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | reports | The two-witness clause explains that one woman may forget the testimony and the other remind her; Ḥamza reads the verb with nominative and gemination under the conditional, while Makki and Baṣri read it accusatively from dhikr.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r2] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | A specified term is a known period, such as harvest, threshing, or the pilgrims' return.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r3] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | Mentioning debt supplies the antecedent for فاكتبوه and clarifies deferred versus immediate debt; the phrasing is more elegant than repeating الدين.

r4] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | Writing a deferred debt is recommended because it better guards against forgetfulness and denial.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r5] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās says this concerns salam; after forbidding usury, God permitted a guaranteed advance sale for a known term and revealed the longest verse, requiring a term for salam.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r6] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | The scribe must be trustworthy and precise, adding nothing and omitting nothing; the debtor's document should be legally valid.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r7] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | The scribe should understand legal conditions, so the parties should select a learned, upright jurist who writes only what Islamic law accepts.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r8] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | No scribe should refuse to write the document as God taught, altering or changing its form.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r9] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | The debtor, as the person liable and subject to testimony, must dictate, making the document his verbal admission; إملال and إملاء are synonymous forms.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r1] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | Witnesses are called witnesses before they testify because the anticipated event is treated as already actual; the first command is obligatory in principle and the second recommended.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r10] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | reports | Witnessing sales is recommended for immediate and deferred exchanges as a precaution, or the command concerns immediate trade alone, where testimony suffices without writing.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r11] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · مكي | reports | Makki reads تذكرة with accusative from dhikr rather than the other derivation.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r12] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · بصري | reports | Baṣri shares the accusative reading تذكرة from dhikr.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r13] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · عمر | reports | ʿUmar reads يضارر in the active voice; Ibn ʿAbbās reads يضار in the passive.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r14] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās reads the passive form ولا يضار, while ʿUmar's active form is ولا يضارر.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r15] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | reports | The active reading forbids a scribe or witness to refuse, distort, add, or omit; the passive forbids burdening them, rushing them from duties, withholding the scribe's fee, or making a witness bear travel costs.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r16] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | Causing such harm is sinful conduct; fear God in this duty, and God teaches the laws of religion without forgetfulness or deficiency.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r2] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · الشاعر | reports | A poet uses s-simt to express becoming weary with life after eighty years, supporting the sense of ولا تسأموا as do not tire.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r3] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | reports | The pronoun in أن تكتبوه may refer to the debt or the document; small or large can describe the debt's value, supporting salam in textiles, or describe a concise or detailed record.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r4] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | Write the debt through its agreed due date; ذلك refers to the act of writing as a verbal noun.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r5] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | Writing is more equitable before God, better supports testimony, and reduces doubt about amount and qualities by providing a written reference.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r6] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | The comparative forms أقسط and أقوم follow Sībawayh's derivation from the causative verbs اقسط and أقام.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r7] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · عاصم | reports | ʿĀṣim reads the phrase so تجارة is the noun of كان or an appositional clarification of trade.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r8] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | reports | Other readings analyze يكون as complete, meaning an immediate transaction occurs, or as incomplete with تجارة حاضرة as its subject and تديرونها as predicate.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r9] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | Managing a spot trade means exchanging it hand to hand; there is no harm in leaving it unwritten because no debt-related suspicion arises.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p138/r1] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | Harming the scribe or witnesses is sinful conduct; fear God in this duty.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p138/r2] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | God teaches the laws of religion and knows everything without forgetfulness or deficiency.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p720#2/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Tadāyantum is a reciprocal verb from debt, applying whether one lends or borrows, as reciprocal sale can mean giving or taking.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · رؤبة | reports | Ruʾba's verse about Arwā paying some debts and delaying others illustrates dāyantu as lending or dealing in debt.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r10] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Rahn is the security given to a creditor; the verbal noun can name the pledged item, and rahana can also mean to remain or continue.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r11] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | reports | Poetry shows rāhin as something retained and arhana as lasting; Ibn Sīda records ra-hana as making something last, while arhana in a sale can mean bidding it up.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r12] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · همام بن مرة وابن الأعرابي والزجاج | reports | Hammām ibn Murra illustrates pledging property with a line; Ibn al-Aʿrābī and al-Zajjāj accept both rahana and arh an a for giving collateral.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r13] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الأعشى | reports | Al-Aʿshā's verse uses rahīna for something pledged, and the author notes rahantu lisānī is said for pledging one's word, not arhantu.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Dāntuhu means I sold to him on credit; adantu means I borrowed on credit.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Amala and amlā are dialect variants for dictating: the first belongs to the Ḥijāz and Banū Asad, the second to Tamīm.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The verb for dictating means casting words for another to write and originally connoted repeating them.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | reports | A poetic line uses umlī to mean wearing something down over time; another account derives the form from amlal with lām changed to yāʾ for ease.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Bakhs means reduction or shortchanging; it can also mean an eye injury, and metaphorically applies to depriving someone of a right or cheating in sale.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Saʾm and saʾāma mean boredom or irritation with something.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r8] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Ṣaghīr is the active participle of ṣaghura and means small in amount, also used for abstract things.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r9] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Qisṭ with kasra means justice or an allotted share; with fatḥa it means injustice.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās says the debt-document verse was revealed specifically about forward-sale transactions in Medina; consensus extends it to all debts.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | After commands to spend in God's path and leave usury, this verse offers a lawful way to grow wealth and gives detailed rules for protecting it.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The word dَayn supplies the pronoun in fa-ktubūhu; it also disambiguates tadāyantum, emphasizes the reference, and generalizes to any size or type of debt.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | A specified term is not a restrictive condition because every valid debt must have a known term; harvest, threshing, or pilgrims' return are too indefinite.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Ila ajal can modify tadāyantum directly or be an adjective phrase for dayn.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r8] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Writing protects against forgetfulness and denial; although its command appears obligatory, the majority treat it as recommended preservation that reduces doubt and supports acknowledgment.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r9] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Writing acts as a substitute for the tongue, just as the tongue conveys what is in the heart.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · أبو سعيد الخدري وابن زيد والشعبي وابن جريج | reports | They held that the trust clause abrogated the command to write; al-Rabīʿ instead says writing was first required and then eased by the trust clause.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r10] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · قيل | reports | A third grammatical view treats bāʾ as extra, yielding the sense let the just scribe write.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · عطاء | reports | ʿAṭāʾ and others say the command that a scribe write is a collective duty, while some say the scribe must write in every circumstance.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الشعبي | reports | Al-Shaʿbī says a scribe must write if no other scribe is available; elsewhere he says the duty applies when the scribe is free.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · السدي | reports | Al-Suddī says writing is obligatory when the scribe has time.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الراغب | prefers | Al-Rāghib prefers a collective duty: the parties need not always document a deal, but a scribe approached for it must write, like a scholar asked to explain a non-obligatory prayer.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Between you means between creditor and debtor, seller and buyer, or lender and borrower; both sh
<<part 37 ends; continues in part 38>>

ould be present so neither side is suspected of dictating a biased record.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Writing justly means truthfully and impartially, without favoring either side in the scribe's mind or pen.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r8] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhsharī attaches bi-l-ʿadl to kātib: the scribe must be trustworthy, write evenly, and know legal conditions, so the parties should select a learned, pious writer.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r9] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن عطية | reports | Ibn ʿAṭiyya attaches the preposition to yaktub rather than kātib: even a child or enslaved person can write a sound deed if legally informed, though officials must choose just, trusted scribes.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · القفال | reports | Al-Qaffāl says justice requires wording accepted by legal scholars and not so ambiguous that a judge could find grounds to invalidate the document.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r10] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الربيع والضحاك | reports | Al-Rabīʿ and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say the ban on a scribe refusing was abrogated by the later ban on harming a scribe or witness.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r11] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The debtor must dictate because the debt is owed from him and the written record safeguards the obligation against him.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الحسن | reports | Al-Ḥasan reads the imperative lām in wa-lyaktub with kasra, its original vowel.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The prohibition lā yaʾba kātib an yaktub forbids a scribe from refusing to write.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Because kātib is indefinite under a prohibition, the command is general.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | On the apparent reading, as God taught him means to write documentation as taught, without alteration; it urges the scribe to use his full knowledge of its conditions.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | reports | Another gloss takes ʿallamahu as made known and understands the phrase as writing in the way God commanded, in truth.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | reports | A further gloss makes the kaaf causal: write because God favored you with the skill, as in the command to do good because God did good to you. | mentions 28:77
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r8] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | prefers | The kaaf most naturally modifies an yaktub; ending the clause there and attaching it to fa-lyaktub is awkward because of the fa and the reversed order.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r9] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن عطية | reports | Ibn ʿAṭiyya suggests as may instead qualify the refusal: just as God gave the scribe writing, he should not refuse and should favor others; the author says this is not the apparent reading.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Pairing Allah with Lord reminds the debtor that God nurtures, repairs, and favors him; Allah comes first because divine authority precedes the reminder of favors.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r10] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · مجاهد والسدي | reports | Mujāhid and al-Suddī also describe the weak person as a fool; others say a minor or one with diminished faculties.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r11] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الطبري | reports | Al-Ṭabarī says weak refers to someone unable to dictate because of speech difficulty or muteness.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r12] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās says inability to dictate can come from speech difficulty, muteness, or absence; others mention madness, ignorance of the account, or childhood.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r13] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | prefers | The three categories are distinct: safīh is profligate or poor at managing money, weak has bodily impairment from childhood or advanced age, and inability to dictate is speech impairment or muteness.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r14] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | rejects | The author rejects claims that either or is redundant, since the coordinating particle is not added without meaning.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r15] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الزمخشري | reports | The author's preferred distinctions largely follow al-Zamakhsharī's explanation.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The debtor must not diminish any amount through deception or resistance; the person ordered to dictate is assumed to control himself.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | reports | Breaking the doubled lām in yumlil is a Ḥijāzī form when the final syllable is jussive or at pause, not in nominative or accusative; one reading doubles shayʾan's yāʾ.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · مجاهد وابن جبير | reports | Mujāhid and Ibn Jubayr define safīh as someone ignorant of practical matters and dictation.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الحسن | reports | Al-Ḥasan says safīh means a child or a woman.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الضحاك والسدي | reports | Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and al-Suddī interpret safīh as a minor.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الشافعي | reports | Al-Shāfiʿī defines safīh as someone who squanders wealth and corrupts his religion.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r8] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās says safīh is one ignorant of Islam; other glosses call him a fool or someone who does not value or grow money.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r9] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن عباس وابن جبير | reports | They interpret ḍaʿīf as an incapacitated person, a mute, or someone mentally impaired.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p726/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن عطية | reports | The verse covers three recurrent cases: the financially incompetent spendthrift, the mentally deficient, and one unable to dictate because absent or ill; their guardians are respectively a guardian or executor, father or executor, and agent, with the mute among the weak or unable.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p726/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Emphasizing “he himself” removes a possible figurative reading and specifies that the debtor cannot dictate personally.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p726/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | reports | A rare reading quiesces the hāʾ of huwa after a word ending in a vowel, treating a separated form like a connected one; this is more exceptional than a reading after thumma.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p726/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | prefers | The pronoun in “his guardian” refers to the debtor, one of the three vulnerable cases; al-Zamakhsharī identifies an executor, agent, or interpreter who dictates with the debtor's approval.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p726/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الطبري | reports | Al-Ṭabarī takes the pronoun to refer to the debt, making the guardian the creditor; this is also related from Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Rabīʿ.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p726/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن عطية، الراغب | rejects | Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects attributing the creditor-as-guardian view to Ibn ʿAbbās because a creditor's dictation cannot establish a debt against a spendthrift; al-Rāghib likewise says a claimant's assertion has no force.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p726/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The bāʾ in “with justice” may attach to the dictation verb or mark its state or manner.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p727/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | “With justice” urges fairness toward both creditor and ward; the verse supports legal interdiction of a minor and transactions by a spendthrift under guardianship.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p727/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | “Seek two witnesses” is a request for testimony or equivalent to “make two witnesses”; shahīd is intensive, suggesting experienced witnesses whose repeated use indicates acceptance and integrity.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p727/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Addressing believers as “your men” indicates non-Muslims are not witnesses here; the verse does not address testimony among non-Muslims, which Abū Ḥanīfa allows even across religions. It also indicates adult male witnesses.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p727/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · شريح، ابن سيرين، ابن شبرمة، عثمان البتي | reports | They accept a slave's testimony; reports also attribute acceptance to ʿAlī, with Ibrāhīm permitting testimony in trivial matters and Anas saying he knows no one who rejected it.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p727/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الجمهور | reports | The majority, including leading Ḥanafīs, Mālik, and al-Shāfiʿī, reject slave testimony in all matters; this is also narrated from ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās, and al-Ḥasan.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p727/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الثوري، أبو حنيفة وأصحابه، ابن شبرمة، الشافعي | reports | They say children's testimony is not considered; Ibn Abī Laylā permits children's mutual testimony, and Mālik permits it in injuries under conditions.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p728/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The apparent requirement is simply that the two principal witnesses be men; jurists disagree over testimony by a blind witness.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p728/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · أبو حنيفة، محمد | reports | They categorically reject testimony by a blind witness; the same view is narrated from ʿAlī, al-Ḥasan, Ibn Jubayr, and Iyās b. Muʿāwiya.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p728/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن أبي ليلى، أبو يوسف، الشافعي، زفر، شريح، الشعبي، مالك، الليث | reports | They differ: Ibn Abī Laylā, Abū Yūsuf, and al-Shāfiʿī accept testimony learned before blindness; Zufar permits only lineage; Shurayḥ and al-Shaʿbī accept it generally; Mālik and al-Layth rely on voice recognition in some matters but reject testimony in adultery or false accusation.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p728/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | reports | Some accept a mute witness through gestures and so
<<part 38 ends; continues in part 39>>

<<2:282 notes, part 39 of 0..65>>
me reject the testimony; deaf witnesses are rejected for spoken claims but accepted for other sensory matters.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p728/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · مالك | reports | Reports from Mālik restrict a Bedouin's testimony against a settled person to injuries, with another report allowing specified travel-related testament and sale cases.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p728/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | “If the two are not men” may mean the creditor failed or chose not to obtain two men; another view requires that two men be unavailable before two women may be called.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p728/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | “One man and two women” admits several ellipses and parses: an omitted witness, a subject with omitted predicate, or a man as subject or passive object of an implied verb.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729#2/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · أبو حنيفة | reports | Abū Ḥanīfa accepts one upright woman's testimony for moon sighting as information, and also accepts a midwife alone.

[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p731/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن أبي ليلى، أبو حنيفة، أبو يوسف، محمد | reports | They accept upright witnesses from sectarian groups except the Khaṭṭābiyya among the Rāfiḍa; Muḥammad rejects Kharijites but accepts Ḥarūriyya because he distinguishes their treatment of Muslims' property.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p731/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · أبو حنيفة، إياس بن معاوية، بلال بن أبي بردة، عمر بن عبد العزيز، شريح، أبو هريرة، محمد | reports | Reports reject witnesses for miserliness, sea-trading, eating clay, plucking or hiding the beard, answering a disparaging nickname, slave dealing, frivolity, effeminacy, or flying pigeons; Shurayḥ's anecdote illustrates the nickname ruling.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p731/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن أبي ليلى، مالك | reports | Ibn Abī Laylā rejects a poor witness because poverty may prompt desire for money; Mālik rejects beggars in substantial matters but accepts testimony in trivial ones.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p731/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الشافعي | reports | One report rejects a witness whose usual conduct is sinful or indecent; another accepts one whose usual conduct is obedience and who has committed no major sin.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p731/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Muruwwa means restraint, dignified bearing, respect for social obligations, and avoiding vulgarity and frivolity, not fine clothing, mounts, tools, or appearance.

[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732#2/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الجمهور | reports | Most readers use subjunctive an and coordinate fa-tudhakkira; Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr lighten the kāf, while others double it.

[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#10/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الجرجاني | reports | Al-Jurjani estimates مخافة أن تضل and cites Amr's verse; the author says this works alone, but فتذكر makes it mistakenly mean fearing that she reminds.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#10/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · أبو جعفر | reports | Abu Ja'far reports that al-Abbas estimated كراهة أن تضل; Abu Ja'far calls it mistaken because it makes the desired reminder something disliked.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#11/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الفراء | reports | Al-Farraʾ estimates كي تذكر إحدى الأخرى إن ضلت, with the result fronted and أن opened; his analogy is delighting in giving a petitioner when asked.

[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#11/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · ابن كثير وأبو عمرو | reports | They lighten the kāf and read فتذكر with accusative rāʾ from أذكرته, meaning to make someone recall after forgetting; ضلال means forgetting, supported by 26:20 and al-Farazdaq. | mentions 26:20
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#11/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | Because أذكرته is causative and takes two objects, the omitted second is testimony: one woman reminds the other of her testimony after forgetting.

[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#12/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · المفسرون وأهل اللسان | rejects | Exegetes and linguists reject the male-equivalence interpretation: forgetting pairs naturally with reminding, it does not fit the testimony rule's male witness, and it would imply wider legal equivalence.

[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#12/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الزمخشري | rejects | Zamakhshari calls making one woman a male witness a far-fetched interpretation, without limiting the criticism to one reading.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#12/r6] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | Nominative فتذكر is coordinated to أن تضل in the readings with أن; only Hamza raises the rāʾ, and the readers divide into three combinations of إن/أن, light/doubled kāf, and case.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | The second object is omitted in this reading too; فعل and أفعل can be synonymous, while the more common doubled form is witnessed by the poet's يذكرنيك.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · عيسى بن عمر والجحدري | reports | They read تضل in the passive; al-Jahdari also reads tuḍillu, from أضل, with the omitted object الشهادة.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · حميد بن عبد الرحمن ومجاهد | reports | They read فتذكر with light kāf and nominative rāʾ.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · زيد بن أسلم | reports | Zayd ibn Aslam reads فتذاكر, the reciprocal form of mutual reminding.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | إحداهما is normally the subject and الأخرى the object, which grammar requires when case is unmarked; semantic clarity can also permit reversing them here.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r6] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · أبو البقاء | reports | Abu al-Baqa says either woman can be parsed as subject because the semantic roles are recoverable, despite the usual ordering rule.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r7] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | The repeated إحداهما rather than a pronoun preserves ambiguity because either woman may forget and remind; the generic wording means if one forgets, the other reminds.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r8] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · أبو البقاء | reports | Abu al-Baqa gives two reasons for repeating the apparent noun: preserve role ambiguity, or replace a pronoun whose reference would make the forgetter also the reminder.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#14/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الفارسي | reports | Al-Farisi analyzes إحدى as an irregular feminine of الواحد; the author prefers it as the regular feminine of أحد, paired in eleven and twenty-one.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#14/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · أبو العباس | reports | إحدى pluralizes as إحد, like كسرة/كسر, because its final alif functions like feminine tāʾ; similar patterns include الكبرى/كبر and قصعاء/قواصع.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#14/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · ابن الأعرابي | reports | Ibn al-A'rabi cites إحدى الإحد as a poetic plural and notes expressions إحدى الإحد, أحد الأحدين, and واحد الآحاد for a unique one.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#14/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | إحدى is used only in annexation, unlike its masculine counterpart أحد.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#14/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | الأخرى is feminine of comparative آخر and can mean آخرة, as in 7:38; both forms pluralize أخر, but their declension and meanings differ. | mentions 7:38
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | The omitted object of ‘refuse’ is establishing the testimony.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r10] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الزمخشري | reports | Zamakhshari says the pronoun may refer to the written document understood from ‘write it.’
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r11] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | ‘Small or large’ is circumstantial: either the debt is small or large, or the written record is brief or detailed.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r12] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · السجاوندي | reports | Al-Sajawandi treats ‘small or large’ as the predicate of an implied kāna; the author says this is unnecessary and unsupported here.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r13] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · السلمي | reports | Al-Sulami reads both verbs with third-person yāʾ; the subject can be the witnesses.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r14] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | On the yāʾ reading, the subject may instead shift to the contracting parties or the scribe.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | Alternatively, ‘refuse’ takes a deleted preposition because it means ‘refrain’; the sense is refraining from

 establishing testimony.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | ‘When they are summoned’ can be a temporal adverb modifying ‘refuse,’ meaning when called to perform or establish testimony.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | The phrase may instead be purely temporal, without conditional force.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | Alternatively, it is conditional, with an omitted answer: when called, they should not refuse.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r6] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | The infinitive clause is the direct object of ‘tire,’ which is directly transitive; a poetic line supports this construction.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r7] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | Another analysis supplies the preposition min before the infinitive; a second poem shows ‘tire’ used with min.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r8] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | Saʾam and saʾāma mean weariness, boredom, and annoyance with something.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r9] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | prefers | The pronoun in ‘write it’ may refer to the debt or the right; the latter is nearer, though it also means the debt.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | prefers | The phrase ‘until its term’ most clearly modifies an implied phrase: the debt remains established in liability until it falls due.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · أبو البقاء | reports | Abu al-Baqa attaches ‘until its term’ directly to ‘write it.’
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الشيخ | rejects | The Shaykh rejects attachment to ‘write’: writing ends quickly and does not continue until the debt is due.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · أبو البقاء | reports | A third analysis makes the phrase a circumstantial clause referring to the pronoun in ‘write it.’
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | prefers | ‘That’ may refer only to writing, to writing and testimony, or to all the preceding instructions; the broadest reference is best.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r6] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | One derivation takes ‘more equitable’ from quadriliteral aqsaṭ, ‘act justly’; this makes the hamza privative but requires an anomalous comparative from a quadriliteral.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r7] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الزمخشري | reports | Zamakhshari says the comparatives may derive from aqsaṭ and aqāma, or from nisba forms meaning ‘possessing equity’ and ‘upright.’
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r8] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الشيخ | rejects | The Shaykh says Sibawayh did not explicitly state that comparatives derive from quadrilaterals; this is inferred from his rules for the exclamative form.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r9] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | Grammarians differ among unrestricted permission, unrestricted prohibition, and permission only when the hamza is not causative; the last reading explains Sibawayh.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · ابن عطية | reports | Ibn Atiyya derives aqsaṭ from the triliteral qasuṭ with ḍamma, like akram from karuma.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r10] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | Aqwam may come from transitive aqāma with its extra hamza removed, meaning firmer for establishing testimony; the analogy is 18:12. | mentions 18:12
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r11] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · أبو البقاء | reports | Abu al-Baqa derives aqwam from intransitive qāma, meaning that testimony itself is more firmly established.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r12] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | The lām in ‘for testimony’ attaches to aqwam and is semantically an object; it is extra if aqwam means ‘establish,’ but not if it means ‘be established.’
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r13] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | The lām cannot normally be dropped to make its complement an accusative after a comparative, except under poetic necessity.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | Another derivation takes it from qist, ‘justice,’ a noun without a verb; this avoids deriving a comparative from ifʿāl.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | These etymologies assume the triliteral means injustice and the quadriliteral means justice.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · سعيد بن جبير | reports | When al-Hajjaj asked his judgment, Saʿid b. Jubayr called him ‘qāsiṭ, ʿādil,’ making a pointed double-edged description. | mentions 72:15, 6:1
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | If q-s-ṭ can mean both justice and injustice, the ambiguity is straightforward; Ibn al-Qattaʿ records both opposite senses.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r6] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · أبو عبيدة | reports | Abu Ubayda, as cited through Ibn al-Sikkit, distinguishes qasaṭ as injustice or justice by vocalization, while aqsaṭ always means justice.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r7] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الراغب الأصفهاني | reports | Al-Raghib says taking another’s share is qist and injustice, while giving that share is iqsaṭ and fairness.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r8] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | ‘With God’ is an adverb modifying ‘more equitable,’ meaning in God’s judgment.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r9] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | The wāw in aqwam is valid because a comparative can follow the pattern of the exclamative, which functions like a noun.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#18/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | The cited poetic phrase has an accusative after a comparative; one analysis supplies an implied verb indicated by the comparative.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#18/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | ‘So that you do not doubt’ has a deleted preposition; proposed choices are lām, ilā, or min, but min does not fit the sense.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#18/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | Tartābū is form VIII from rayba; its original yāʾ becomes alif because it is vowelled after an open syllable.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#18/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | The comparison’s second term is omitted because context supplies it: writing is more equitable, stable, and doubt-free than leaving the debt undocumented.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#18/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | Omission is smoother when the comparative is a predicate than when it is an adjective or circumstantial phrase.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#18/r6] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · السلمي | reports | Al-Sulami reads the clause with third-person yāʾ, matching his reading of ‘they tire of writing.’
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · أبو البقاء | reports | Abu al-Baqa treats the trade exception as connected: from all transactions requiring testimony, it excludes the case of present trade.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · مكي ابن أبي طالب | reports | Makki b. Abi Talib calls the exception disconnected; the author prefers this reading as the apparent sense, permitting omission of writing and witnesses for immediate trade.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | ʿAsim reads ‘trade’ and its adjective in the accusative; in al-Nisaʾ the two other Kūfan readers agree, while the rest read both nominative. | mentions 4:29
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | With nominative, kāna may be complete, meaning a trade occurs; ‘you circulate it’ is then an adjectival clause, a more idiomatic order.

[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r8] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | rejects | The author says al-Farisi’s objection does not answer al-Zajjaj, since trade too is a verbal noun and thus an abstract meaning.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r9] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الفارسي | reports | Al-Farisi also rules out ‘the right’ as kāna’s subject because it is a debt, so an omitted subject must be supplied.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#2/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | إلى أجل is emphatic because debt is necessarily deferred; مسمى's alif comes from yāʾ, itself from waw in the root.

[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#2/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhshari attaches بالعدل to كاتب as its adjective, meaning a trustworthy writer.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#2/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · ابن عطية | prefers | Ibn Atiyya attaches the bā to وليكتب, not كاتب, since a child or slave may write a document even if not personally just.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#2/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | A third analysis makes باء extra, yielding كاتب العدل, the just writer.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#20/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | One possible omitted subject of kāna is ‘transaction,’ understood from the preceding commands; Sibawayh gives a similar contextual ellipsis.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#20/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | A poem using ‘when there was stabbing and embracing’ supplies an omitted ‘matter’ as the subject of kāna.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#20/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الفراء | reports | Another analysis supplies ‘trade’ twice: ‘unless there is trade, as a trade’; al-Farraʾ and al-Zamakhshari cite poetic parallels with an understood repeated noun.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:282#20/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | ‘Between you’ is an adverb modifying ‘you circulate it.’

item.text: The later commentaries add detailed legal subquestions about witness eligibility, testimony with an oath, fixed terms in advance sales, and whether a document can support a witness whose memory has faded. I’m keeping these as distinct questions where the notes give distinct rulings.
